postings.title: Lifecycle Marketing Manager
postings.descriptionText:
Lifecycle Marketing Manager
Remote (minimum 4-hour overlap with US Eastern hours) | Marketing | Reports to: Director, Revenue Marketing
Time Doctor is hiring a Lifecycle Marketing Manager to own the marketing-led customer journey from the moment an account starts paying. You will decide who hears what, when, based on which behaviour, and toward which commercial outcome. Your job is to turn customer behaviour and usage signals into adoption, retention, expansion and reactivation revenue, and to run that engine AI-first, building agents and agentic workflows that do real work.

Who we are
Time Doctor is a workforce analytics platform that gives distributed teams the visibility they need to improve trust and performance. We serve remote, hybrid and outsourced organisations worldwide, with particular strength in BPO, healthcare and tech services. We are bootstrapped, profitable and fully remote, with team members across 30+ countries. We built a durable business on customer revenue rather than venture capital, and we are now focused on growing it.

The role
You will own the lifecycle marketing program for our paying customers: the 30/60/90 onboarding plays, ongoing customer communications, customer segmentation, and the expansion and retention plays that grow and keep the base. You design the journeys, brief the work, QA it and measure it, and you own the revenue outcome.

Three things define this seat.

• The number. Your primary measure is the qualified expansion and cross-sell opportunities Lifecycle generates and surfaces. Expansion revenue, net revenue retention and at-risk recovery sit right behind it, shared with CS, Sales and Product.

• The lane. You own orchestration and outcomes across the customer base, not every surface you touch. PMM owns the message, GTM Ops builds the scoring and routing, and Growth and CS co-define the signals with you. You make it all work together.

• The operating model. This is an AI-first role, and AI fluency is the job. The bar is that you can stand up an agent that does real work, not describe one. Accelerating Time Doctor 's AI-first operating model is an explicit expectation of the seat.

This is a systems role. You build repeatable, automated journeys rather than one-off campaigns, and you keep human ownership of segmentation logic, offer design, guardrails, final QA and the commercial call.

Who you are

• You treat a revenue number as yours, and you design every journey toward adoption, retention or expansion.

• You have high agency. When a journey underperforms, you find out why and fix it.

• You are commercially minded. You turn customer signals into revenue.

• You are analytical and cohort-fluent. You read behaviour and act on where customers stall or grow.

• You think in systems. You would rather build a repeatable, automated flow than run another one-off campaign.

• You work cleanly across Growth, CS, PMM and GTM Ops without needing to own their surfaces, and you turn ambiguous boundaries into working agreements.

• You build with AI. Agents and agentic workflows are how you get work done.

What you will own

• Onboarding and adoption. The marketing-led 30/60/90 program that gets new paying customers to first value, plus ongoing adoption of key capabilities and education, including driving traffic to TD Academy and running education webinars end to end. You own the day-0 handoff: the trigger and the data that enrol a new customer in the right journey.

• Segmentation and journey orchestration. Segmenting paying customers on profile, product usage, engagement, lifecycle stage, adoption state, expansion propensity and churn risk, then designing, building and QA-ing the journeys and triggers on top, so the right cohort gets the right play at the right moment.

• Expansion and cross-sell. Plays that grow existing accounts through seats, add-ons and cross-sell. You co-define expansion signals with Growth and CS, turn them into segments and plays, and route qualified opportunities to Sales and CS, with GTM Ops implementing detection and actions.

• Retention and win-back. Proactive plays against at-risk cohorts, air cover for CS retention efforts, re-engagement of dormant accounts, and win-back of churned accounts where it is commercially worthwhile.

• Renewal-moment marketing. Value-recap and air-cover campaigns timed to the renewal window, reinforcing realised value ahead of the CS conversation.

• Customer communications. Audience, segmentation, timing and orchestration for the customer newsletter, customer webinars, feature and release comms, and lifecycle-triggered in-app announcements. PMM owns the message. You own distribution.

• Advocacy and review sites. Identifying advocates and triggering review, referral, testimonial and reference asks at the right lifecycle moment, including activating the promoters CS surfaces through NPS. You fully own review-site management and take the case studies Content and PMM produce to market.

• Lifecycle analytics and experimentation. Performance across every journey, from onboarding completion and time-to-value through to expansion, retention, renewal support and win-back. You find where customers stall, drop off, expand or disengage, and you keep improving the programs.

• AI in the workflow. Agentic workflows for segmentation, usage and account signal interpretation, journey and trigger build and testing, customer comms drafting and variants, propensity and churn scoring drafts, cohort analysis and drop-off detection. You decide what runs autonomously, what needs human judgement, and how each workflow gets operationalised with GTM Ops.

This role may not suit you if

• You measure yourself on sends, opens and campaign volume rather than on revenue adopted, kept and grown.

• You prefer launching one-off campaigns to building journeys that run on their own.

• AI for you means prompt libraries and screenshots. We need someone who has built agents that do real work.

• Your experience is mostly top-of-funnel. This role starts the moment an account becomes a paying customer.

• You need to own every surface you touch. PMM owns the message and GTM Ops builds the scoring and routing, and this seat depends on working well with both.

• You cannot commit to at least four hours a day of overlap with US Eastern business hours.

What a realistic week looks like
A cohort review showing where last month's new customers stalled before day 30, and a fix to the onboarding journey that ships the same week. A working session with CS on an at-risk cohort and the play you will run against it. Two expansion opportunities your signals surfaced, qualified and routed to Sales. An agent you built to draft and QA journey variants, tightened after its first run. A value-recap campaign going out to accounts entering their renewal window. Live collaboration during US Eastern hours, async for the rest of the day.

Requirements

Your experience

• 5 to 7 years in lifecycle, CRM, customer or retention marketing at a B2B SaaS company.

• A track record of designing and running behaviour-triggered customer journeys, with adoption, retention or expansion outcomes you owned. You know your numbers and can walk us through them.

• Comfortable working from product-usage and account data to define segments, propensity and churn logic. You can specify the scoring and routing, even though GTM Ops builds it.

• Fluent in a marketing automation or lifecycle stack such as HubSpot, and in cohort analysis.

• Experience running expansion, cross-sell or renewal-support programs, and coordinating opportunity handoff with CS and Sales.

• A clear understanding of where lifecycle ends and Growth and CS begin, and the ability to work cleanly across those lines.

• Hands-on experience building agents or agentic workflows that do real work. You can show us what you built and what it does.

• Remote, with a minimum four-hour daily overlap with US Eastern (ET) business hours.

Nice to have

•
Product-led SaaS experience.

• More than four hours of daily overlap with US Eastern business hours.

• Background in workforce analytics, time tracking, HR tech or productivity software.

• Experience marketing to BPO, outsourcing, healthcare or tech services customers.

The team you are joining
You will report to our Director, Revenue Marketing. You will work closely with Growth and CS on expansion and churn signals, with PMM and Content on messaging and proof assets, with GTM Ops on scoring, routing and journey implementation, and with Sales and CS on the opportunities you hand forward.

How we will measure success

• Qualified expansion and cross-sell opportunities you generate and surface. This is the headline measure and the one you control most directly.

• Expansion revenue, net revenue retention contribution and at-risk recovery, which CS, Sales and Product also influence.

• Onboarding completion, time-to-value and product adoption depth among paying customers, as the leading indicators.

• Advocacy volume across reviews, referrals and references, renewal-support coverage, and revenue recovered through win-back.

Your first 90 days

• Days 1 to 30. Map the post-conversion journey and where customers stall. Audit the current 30/60/90 onboarding and customer comms. Document the conversion handoff: the trigger and the data that must travel with a new customer. Agree the first expansion and churn signals with Growth and CS, and baseline adoption, retention and expansion.

• Days 31 to 60. Launch or repair the 30/60/90 onboarding. Stand up the first expansion play and one renewal-moment campaign. Set up cohort reporting, introduce AI-assisted segmentation and comms, and get review-site management and one advocacy trigger (NPS promoters from CS) live.

• Days 61 to 90. Scale the expansion and retention plays that are working. Run a win-back pilot. Establish expansion-opportunity routing to Sales and CS with GTM Ops, then present the adoption, retention and expansion baseline alongside a lifecycle roadmap.

Why this role

• You own a real revenue number, from the moment a customer converts.

• You get a clear lane. Growth, CS, PMM and GTM Ops are your partners, and your focus is orchestration and outcomes.

• You work AI-first from day one, at a company where accelerating an AI-first operating model is an explicit expectation.

• We are profitable and bootstrapped. Your budget comes from customers, not from a burn rate.

postings.descriptionText:
Hi, I'm Paul, VP of Engineering at Customer.io . We're looking for a staff product engineer — not a generalist who happens to touch frontend and backend, but someone who thinks like a product owner and ships like an engineer.

About Customer.io

Over 9,000 companies — from scrappy startups to global brands — use our platform to send billions of emails, push notifications, in-app messages, and SMS every day. Customer.io powers automated communication that people actually want to receive.
We help teams send smarter, more relevant messages using real-time behavioral data. Under the hood: Go, React, and AI help us ship fast and scale with confidence.

What We Value

End-to-end ownership
You take on the problems nobody's claimed — the ones that span squads with no obvious owner — and carry them from a fuzzy first conversation to what's actually live. If it touches the customer, it's yours to chase down.

Comfort in ambiguity
Half-formed problems and conflicting signals are your starting material, not a blocker. You define the problem before you solve it, form a point of view on what's worth building, and move without waiting for someone else to de-risk the call.

Customer-first, always
You think from the customer's problem backward, not the codebase forward. Every technical call traces back to what it does for the person on the other end of the message — and you can explain that connection to people who don't write code. Given the choice, you ship the thing that changes their experience, not the thing that's merely elegant.

A healthy skepticism for "the way things are done"
You retire practices that have outlived their usefulness, including ones you helped build. Best practices matter — but never more than forward motion.

Force multiplication
Shipping your part isn't the bar. You bring in the right people before a problem becomes theirs to clean up, and you leave enough behind — docs, patterns, delegation — that the team keeps moving without you in the room.

What You'll Do

• Own important, ambiguous problems from initial framing through launch and iteration. Set direction, align partners, and stay accountable for the result.

• Partner with product, design, and data to shape priorities, scope the work, and define how success will be measured.

• Lead technical decisions across the stack, including architecture, performance, reliability, and maintainability.

• Lead work across teams and systems. Build alignment, resolve technical disagreements, and keep complex initiatives moving.

• Improve engineering practices through mentorship, reusable patterns, and clear technical guidance.

• Use AI throughout your engineering work, with sound judgment about where it helps, where it falls short, and how its output should be reviewed. Help the team improve by testing new workflows, sharing what works, and identifying useful opportunities for automation.

• Participate in an on-call rotation as required, supporting the systems the team builds.

What we're looking for

• A track record of leading complex work across teams or systems and delivering meaningful customer, business, or engineering outcomes.

• Strong backend engineering experience, with the ability to work across the stack and lead end-to-end technical decisions.

• Strong product and technical judgment, especially when the problem or path forward is unclear.

• The ability to influence experienced peers and align teams without formal authority.

• Experience using metrics, experimentation, and observability to guide decisions and improve production systems.

• Regular, hands-on use of AI across the software development lifecycle, with the judgment to adapt as tools change while remaining accountable for quality, security, and outcomes. Experience improving how a broader team uses AI is a strong plus.

Compensation & Benefits
We believe in transparency. Starting salary for this role is $200,000 - $280,000 USD (or equivalent in local currency) depending on experience and subject to market rate adjustment. This role also carries a 10% annual bonus target.
We know our people are what make us great, and we're committed to taking great care of them. Our inclusive benefits package supports your well-being and growth, including 100% coverage of medical, dental, vision, mental health, and supplemental insurance premiums for you and your family. We also offer 16 weeks paid parental leave, unlimited PTO, stipends for remote work and wellness, a professional development budget, and more.
See full benefits here →

Our Process
No gotchas, no trick questions - just a clear, human process designed to help both of us make an informed decision.

•
Application - We review everyone with care. Tell us why you're interested.

•
Recruiter Call (30 mins) - Let's chat about what you're looking for and how we work.

•
Hiring Manager Interview (60 mins) - Talk with one of our hiring managers about your working style and a product you've owned end-to-end, plus a short AI-assisted coding exercise.

System Design Interview (60 mins) - A collaborative conversation that moves between product tradeoffs and system design — how you'd scope something ambiguous and how you'd build it.

•
Take-Home Assignment - Complete a short, realistic task similar to what you'd work on here.

•
Assignment Review Call (60 mins) - Walk us through your work and discuss tradeoffs, priorities, and how you'd iterate.

All final candidates will be asked to complete a background check and employment verifications as part of our pre-employment process.

• Own cross-channel CRM communication across email, push, in-app messages, website or platform touchpoints, chat, WhatsApp / messengers, and sales or support touchpoints where relevant.

• Monitor and report performance of CRM flows and campaigns, using data to identify what should be improved, scaled or stopped.

Requirements
5+ years of experience in CRM, lifecycle marketing, retention marketing, customer engagement or a similar area.

Strong understanding of customer lifecycle mechanics: onboarding, activation, engagement, retention, churn prevention and reactivation.

Strong business and customer thinking: ability to understand what kind of message, hook, content or channel is likely to work for a specific client segment.

Ability to work independently, structure work clearly and take ownership of outcomes under a service agreement model.

Experience building CRM programmes from an early or underdeveloped stage.

Co-Founding CEO (Metabolic & Inflammation Therapies)
Location: Remote
Commitment: Part-time to start, with greater time commitment expected as the company scales
Compensation : Equity only, transitioning to salary after fundraising
Start Date : ASAP preferred, Q4 2026 at the latest
Seniority : Co-founder / Leadership

About the Company
This startup is developing a new kind of small molecule to treat diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and other metabolic diseases.
Their approach is different from existing treatments: instead of managing symptoms (like blood sugar or blood pressure), their drug targets the root cause: a molecular signal inside cells that triggers inflammation and scarring in the kidneys.
Their lead drug, INT-101, is first-in-class and acts by blocking a specific interaction between two proteins (RAGE and DIAPH1). Blocking this interaction mitigates the downstream effects that lead to kidney inflammation and fibrosis. As a result, it has the potential to restore kidney function, not just slow the damage. No other current therapies have this disease-modifying effect.
Built on Professor Ann Marie Schmidt's pioneering RAGE biology research at NYU, the platform shows strong preclinical proof-of-concept in diabetic kidney disease and potential across multiple indications. With four granted U.S. patents, it represents a credible, first-in-class therapeutic approach moving toward clinical development.

Purpose of the Role
The CEO will lead all aspects of the venture's growth, from setting strategy to advancing its first programs into clinical trials.
This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who combines scientific understanding with strong business and fundraising skills. The CEO will decide the indication strategy, secure new funding, build and lead the team, and represent the company to investors, partners, and the broader biotech community.
This is a unique opportunity to shape a first-in-class biotech from the ground up, driving a platform with potential impact across multiple chronic diseases.

Key Responsibilities

• Define and execute the company's strategy, aligning science, operations, and business goals.

• Choose and prioritize indication strategy (such as DKD, obesity, atherosclerosis, or MASH) based on opportunity, patient need, and risk.

At INDG , we create photoreal digital content for brands like Adidas, On Running, Puma, Wilson, and Hugo Boss. We're looking for a Technical CG Lead to supervise and own the technical side of how we get there - across CGI, AI, pipeline, and process. You see the whole picture, from how one artist works to how the whole production runs, and you'd rather fix something yourself than wait for someone else to. If you've spent years thinking "there's a better way to do this," we'd love to hear from you.

About INDG

INDG brings together two decades of CGI expertise with our own technology - large-scale CGI content, digital twins, and automated content for brands across fashion, sportswear, luxury, automotive, and consumer electronics, with teams in Amsterdam, Bucharest, and New York. We value ownership, collaboration, and craft.

What you'll be doing

• Own and improve our technical pipeline - tooling, automation, data flows, and standards.

• Lead the technical team and advise artists and Art Directors on better ways of working.

• Bring focus and direction to our AI exploration.

• Spot bottlenecks early and turn them into scalable fixes.

• Get hands-on when it counts, then turn what works into practice for the wider team.

• Shape the technical and production roles we need as we grow.

• Keep us current and competitive in the ever-evolving world of tech.

Requirements

What we're looking for

• Proven experience in a senior technical role - CG Supervisor, Technical Director, Pipeline Lead, or similar.

• Solid grip on CGI pipelines, DCC tools, rendering, and production.

• Enough scripting know-how to guide developers and make good calls.

• A natural doer with strong systems thinking.

• Curious about AI, and sharp at spotting what's hype.

• Clear communicator across artists, Art Directors, developers, and producers.

Our main tools
C4D, Houdini, Blender, Substance, CLO3D/MD, Browzwear, and Nuke - plus a growing set of AI tools you'll help shape.

The kind of person we're looking for
You care as much about how people use technology as the technology itself - a tool isn't finished until artists are using it and production's genuinely better for it. You'll have authority to shape how our Fashion vertical works - and we expect you to use it.

Why Join INDG

INDG sits between CGI craft, production technology, and enterprise-scale content operations. Grip, our content orchestration platform, supports AI workflows and production-grade output for brands that depend on visual consistency across markets, channels, and product lines.
This role matters because fashion visual production is becoming more systemized, more automated, and more technically demanding. The Challenge
According to the Intergovernmental Panel of Climate Change (IPCC), we have only a decade to make massive and unprecedented changes in the global economy to avoid dangerous climate change. To meet that challenge, Global Energy Monitor is creating trackers and other tools to provide detailed information on energy facilities, sponsors, and financing.

About Global Energy Monitor

Global Energy Monitor (GEM) is a global, independent nonprofit network of researchers tracking energy infrastructure worldwide, from power stations and coal mines to steel plants and shipping terminals, for the worldwide climate and clean energy movement.

postings.descriptionText:
WHO WE ARE
Interdependence is a tech-powered, integrated marketing and communications agency built around one core belief: strategy comes first.
Founded in public relations, we've grown into a full-service partner spanning PR, social media, paid media, brand strategy and consulting, event marketing, influencer marketing, website strategy and development, and integrated marketing planning. Our approach starts with our clients' goals, not a predetermined set of services. When the best solution falls outside our own capabilities, we're willing to say so. Achieving our clients' goals is always the priority.
We combine smart strategy, experienced people and technology, including our Newsweek AI Impact Award-winning Interviewed™ platform, to deliver measurable results. Just as importantly, we believe how we work matters. Kindness, collaboration, curiosity and accountability shape how we partner with our clients and each other. THE MISSION
Help turn client goals into organized, thoughtful marketing programs while becoming a trusted, proactive contributor to the Integrated Marketing & Strategy team.
Our team supports clients across influencer marketing, events, brand strategy and identity, website strategy and development and other integrated marketing needs. Account Executives help connect the client, the strategy and the people responsible for bringing the work to life.
Your job is to keep projects moving, communicate clearly, anticipate what is needed next and help solve problems before they become roadblocks. As you grow in the role, the expectation is that you look beyond assigned tasks, develop stronger client and business judgment, and take greater ownership of day-to-day work.

THREE PRINCIPLES

•
Client goals come first. Start with what the client needs to accomplish, then help determine the channels, partners and next steps best positioned to support that goal.

•
Stay one step ahead. Do not wait to be asked for the obvious next step. Keep the team informed, flag risks early and think about what the client or project will need next.

•
Be curious and resourceful. You will not always have an immediate answer. Ask smart questions, research options, talk to new people and bring forward a recommended path rather than stopping at the problem.

WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT

•
You are not expected to arrive as an expert in every marketing channel. Specific influencer, event, brand or website experience is helpful but not required. You are expected to learn quickly, understand how different disciplines work together and build broader channel knowledge over time.

•
You are not expected to lead client strategy alone. Senior team members own overarching strategy, senior counsel and complex client conversations. You are expected to understand that strategy, contribute ideas and increasingly connect your work to the client's broader goals.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Client & Account Support

Influencer Programs & Events

• Communicate professionally with creators, vendors and new contacts and confidently ask the questions needed to evaluate options or solve problems.

• Provide on-site event and activation support as needed and remain calm, flexible and solutions-focused when plans change.

Creative & Strategic Contribution

• Actively contribute ideas during brainstorms, planning sessions and account discussions.

• Conduct research that helps the team understand audiences, competitors, cultural trends, potential partners and new approaches.

• Show genuine interest in creative work and help move ideas from early concepts through final execution.

• Begin thinking strategically about the client's broader goals and recommend ideas to the account lead that could improve the work or create greater business value.

Team Collaboration & Preparedness

• Partner closely with senior team members, specialists and peers to keep accounts and projects moving efficiently.

• Maintain accurate project trackers, status updates, contact lists, budgets and other working documents.

• Balance multiple priorities and deadlines while communicating early when timing, scope or resources may need to change.

Reporting & Insights

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Project Ownership & Preparedness: You keep timelines, deliverables, approvals and follow-ups organized. You identify next steps, prepare materials with enough lead time for thoughtful review and flag risks or opportunities early.

Team Trust: You become someone senior team members can confidently hand work to knowing it will be moved forward thoughtfully, accurately and on time. You communicate early when you need guidance, take feedback well and apply it to future work.

WHY YOU'LL LOVE WORKING AT INTERDEPENDENCE

postings.title: Cloud DevOps Engineer
postings.descriptionText:
Cloud DevOps Engineer
Azumo builds and operates production AI systems for companies ranging from seed-stage startups to Meta. We are hiring a Cloud DevOps Engineer to own the infrastructure those systems run on: the clusters, the pipelines that deploy to them, and the monitoring that says whether any of it is healthy. The role is fully remote across Latin America, aligned to your client's working day.
You will not be handed a runbook. Azumo has shipped production infrastructure since 2016, and the work here is in systems that are already live: what breaks, what a cluster costs to run, and what nobody has automated yet because it was always easier to do by hand.

Where this role sits
At Azumo , ownership is split by what gets built: the pipelines, the method behind a decision, the product, and what an AI system does once it's live. This role owns what all of it runs on — clusters, deployment, and the infrastructure those systems depend on to stay up.
A system that is down, a slow query nobody escalates, a cluster that costs more than it should: they are all yours. Recovery first, root cause after, and the change that keeps it from happening again.

What you will build

•
Clusters that hold. Kubernetes in production — provisioning, upgrades, networking, and the workload configuration that decides whether a bad deploy takes one service down or all of them.

•
Infrastructure as code. Terraform or equivalent, with environments reproducible from the repository rather than from memory, and drift that gets detected instead of discovered.

•
Delivery pipelines. CI/CD that developers and QA can rely on, container images that are built the same way every time, and deployments to production that are unremarkable.

•
Observability and response. Monitoring and alerting that fires on what matters, plus the investigation, the root cause and the follow-up change when something does break.

•
Infrastructure for AI workloads. The clusters and inference services the AI Engineer lane deploys onto, whether that's hosted APIs or models we run ourselves, with the cost and scaling profile each one brings.

•
Cost and capacity. What the infrastructure costs to run, what it would cost at three times the traffic, and which of the two problems is worth solving now.

•
Hardening. Linux, Kubernetes, containers and the service mesh secured as a default rather than as a project, with secrets, access and audit trails that survive a client's review.

•
Tooling, documentation and support. The internal tooling your own team runs on, the documentation that makes any of it operable by someone else, and the developers and QA you unblock during the release cycle.

•
Work inside the client's environment, when that's the engagement. Some of this work runs on Azumo 's own infrastructure and some inside a client's — their repositories, their cloud account, their change process. Azumo is SOC 2 certified, client code stays in client repositories, and some engagements carry additional requirements such as HIPAA.

How we work
Our engineers build with AI every day. Claude Code, Codex, and similar tools are part of the standard toolchain here, not an experiment. We run an automated audit across the whole codebase on day one and every day after, grading security, cost, and architecture findings by severity with the exact file and line, so a small team can move quickly without quality drifting. We stay vendor-neutral across OpenAI, Anthropic, and open-weight models, and we run Valkyrie, our own production layer, when a single interface to any model is the right call.

About Azumo

Azumo is a San Francisco based software development company that has been building intelligent applications since 2016. We provide nearshore AI engineering teams to organizations that need production AI faster than they can hire for it: as an embedded engineering team, as AI staff augmentation alongside an existing team, or as a full project build. Our engineers work from Latin America, aligned to United States time zones, and have delivered for Twitter, Meta, Discovery Channel, Omnicom, UnitedHealth, and CENTEGIX.
We hire for seniority and test for it before anyone joins a client team. We support engineers in going deep on the modern AI stack, and we give time back to open-source work, community teaching, and philanthropy.
Apply at or write to us at .

Requirements

Basic qualifications

• 5+ years as a DevOps, SRE or systems engineer running production infrastructure, with the fundamentals that go with it: Linux administration, networking, Git, and scripting in Bash plus Python or Go.

• Kubernetes in production, at depth: not only deploying to a cluster someone else built, but provisioning, upgrading and debugging one when it misbehaves.

• Infrastructure as code as your working practice: Terraform or equivalent, with state, modules and environment parity you can defend.

• CI/CD pipelines you built and maintain — GitHub Actions, GitLab or equivalent — and container images you are responsible for.

• Cloud deployment experience on AWS, Azure or GCP, including the managed Kubernetes service and the cost model that comes with it.

• Monitoring and incident work: Datadog, CloudWatch or equivalent, and a track record of taking an incident from alert to root cause to a change that prevented the repeat.

• Security hardening of Linux, containers and Kubernetes as part of how you build, not as a separate phase.

• Working discipline around infrastructure cost and capacity. You can explain what a cluster costs to run and what you did about it.

• Active use of AI-assisted coding tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot in real delivery work.

• Clear written and spoken English, C1 or above, and the confidence to explain a technical trade-off directly to a client.

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

Preferred qualifications

• Service mesh and traffic management: Istio, Linkerd or equivalent, and the failure modes they introduce as well as the ones they solve.

• Helm, Kustomize or an equivalent approach to templating and environment configuration.

• Database operations at production scale: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, RDS, DynamoDB or equivalent.

• Running or scaling inference workloads, and the cost and latency trade-offs against hosted APIs.

• Delivery under a compliance regime such as SOC 2 or HIPAA.

• Cloud certifications, or contributions to open-source infrastructure tooling and published technical writing.

Benefits
100% remote-first culture (work anywhere in Latin America)

Paid time off (PTO)

U.S. Holidays

Solid AI Training and certification

Mentored career development

Profit sharing

$US remuneration

Maternity coverage

postings.title: Enterprise Account Executive
postings.descriptionText:
This is a general track role, hiring for opportunities across all levels of seniority in our Sales Teams.
Apply here if you believe you possess outstanding revenue generating experience from the Technology industry.
Open source software is the new default in the enterprise, and Canonical is the new challenger to major enterprise software vendors.
We deliver better open source from the data center to cloud and edge. Our Linux distribution Ubuntu is now the leading platform for public cloud compute, and the favorite platform for software engineers, data scientists and AI developers. Our mission is to accelerate the adoption and quality of open source globally, and our goal is to ship the most software on the planet by cores. A tidal wave of open source innovation is the next phase of the entire enterprise software industry, and we aim to be the most compelling way to ride that wave.
Our customers include Global 500 enterprises and startups. We are expanding our product range from the base operating system - Ubuntu - to full enterprise solutions in infrastructure and applications. We can deliver software defined storage, private cloud solutions, container runtime environments, as well as databases, message queues, identity, observability, analytics, machine learning and web publishing capabilities. Customers love the idea that they can get security compliance and support for everything open source from a single company. Our goal is to have more solutions on tap than any other vendor, and we have built unique capabilities to make that possible across every cloud, every class of compute and every category of application.
Canonical provides licensed enterprise software products, commercial support, managed services, consulting and training services to customers who are deploying Ubuntu or open source applications on the cloud, in their data center, or to the connected device and IoT ecosystem. We are just over 1,000 colleagues in 70+ countries and $250m in revenue, profitable, on a steady but relentless growth trajectory. We are almost entirely distributed, with leadership spread across many countries. We believe that talent is equally distributed across the globe, and we are excited to hire, develop, promote and ultimately trust a diverse group of exceptional leads to build the best, not biggest, enterprise software company.
We hire carefully and deliberately; our selection process is long and requires substantial work from applicants. It will take successful applicants three to six months to secure an offer. This is not a place to apply if you are in a rush to find a position, it is a worthwhile place to apply if you are ambitious and long-term in your thinking about your career and the dynamics which move the world forward. If you see clearly the rise of open source, and you understand the drivers of enterprise procurement and technical decision making, then you will understand why Canonical has such a tremendous long term advantage. You will also understand, given the ferocity of competition and the challenges of competing in a market of giants, that we have to set a very high bar for hiring and performance. In order to be a world leading company we select for exceptional ability as well as character, and then provide an environment which promotes teamwork and celebrates diligence, collaboration and effectiveness. All of those are easy to say but hard to do - at Canonical we are willing to be uncomfortable in pursuit of that excellence.
In building our sales team, we look for five things:

• Empathy for the customer - a real understanding of customer needs, industry-specific challenges, and a desire to help customers solve their business problems

• High intellect - the ability to learn quickly, understand very complex subjects, and communicate clearly to build trust and confidence

• Passion for technology - a fascination with the state of the art from brilliant people solving hard problems, and fierce competition for large prizes

• Teamwork - a willingness to help others, to collaborate well with people from different disciplines, and to balance personal and team ambitions

• Energy - the drive to motivate oneself and others to achieve the best result for the team and our customers

Ubuntu is already very widely adopted which gives us a credible basis for conversations in the market. Nevertheless, it requires real work for sales professionals to build on that adoption to create trusted and profitable commercial relationships with the enterprises in their territory. Our product managers and marketing teams run campaigns to generate awareness, engagement and leads, but you will need to go beyond managing inbound interest to develop the potential of your territory. You will need judgement as to which industries and companies are ready to go deeper with open source and Canonical, and energy to develop relationships in advance of proven interest. We expect professional practice, territory and account planning, as well as clear, complete and continuous reporting on pipeline status and activity, using standard professional tools.
The successful candidate will carry an annual bookings quota within their assigned territory. They should be able to travel regionally for client engagement, industry conferences, and internationally for company events twice a year. They will be expected to demonstrate professionalism and effectiveness, to prospect accounts for new business, maintain and develop existing relationships, and work with colleagues and partners on account strategy. They must be comfortable selling enterprise software, open source, cloud, virtualization, container technologies and technical software solutions to senior levels of the enterprise.
Location: We are expanding our sales organisation globally and have open roles in every region.

What your day will look like

• Represent the company, its solutions and software, in your territory

• Build and execute a territory plan to prioritize outreach and prospecting

• Develop new pipeline through outreach, prospecting, local marketing, and industry events

• Close contracts to meet and exceed quarterly and annual bookings targets

• Be mindful and proactive in achieving tactical and strategic objectives

• Manage customer relationships and interactions through all stages of the sales cycle

• Work with field engineers to propose solutions that solve our customers’ business problems

• Work with customer success to identify growth opportunities

• Maintain accurate pipeline data and forecasts within Salesforce

• Establish productive professional relationships with key influencers and decision makers

What we are looking for in you

• Bachelor's level degree, preferably in engineering or computer science

• Experience of open source technology and solutions

• Detail oriented with effective follow-up

• Experience in enterprise software or technology sales planning and execution

• Track record of achievement in sales targets and new account wins

• Self-discipline and motivation to be successful in a distributed team

• Professional written and spoken English, as well as any language that may be appropriate for your target market

• Ability to travel for customer engagements, industry events and company events

Additional skills of interest

• Specific vertical experience, in particular finance, telco, health, energy, public sector, tech

• Experience speaking at conferences or industry events

What we offer you
We consider geographical location, experience, and performance when shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognise outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven commission structure. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

• Annual compensation review

• Recognition rewards

• Annual holiday leave

• Maternity and paternity leave

• Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues

• Priority Pass, and travel upgrades for long haul company events

About Canonical
Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world on a daily basis. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Canonical has been a fully distributed company since its inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We're hiring experienced performance engineers to find and land performance wins across the Supabase stack — from the query optimiser to block device level, and across the network paths and cloud infrastructure that connect our distributed platform. This is a performance delivery role: real, measured improvements to our database, platform, and APIs as we scale toward enterprise and platform-grade workloads. The methodologies you develop and tooling you build exist to multiply that delivery.

You'd join a new performance team as one of its first members, working alongside a deeply seasoned performance engineer, with the team growing to roughly six this year. There's no legacy process to inherit — you'll help define how performance engineering works at Supabase.

What you'll do

•
Find bottlenecks in live production systems and characterize them precisely enough that the owning team can act on them without you in the room.

•
Partner closely with database teams (e.g. Multigres, OrioleDB) and infra teams to land concrete performance improvements.

•
Build, communicate, and evolve performance methodologies and tooling that turn live production data into actionable insight.

•
Partner with the observability team to capture the right signals and establish a unified view of platform performance (latency, throughput, tail behavior) across products.

•
Help teams self-serve performance analysis and make performance a first-class engineering concern.

Problems you might work on

•
Tune the kernel's paging behavior to production workloads

•
Reduce memory overhead in OrioleDB and Multigres

•
Identify and eliminate sources of latency spikes from application to kernel level

•
Identify scalability bottlenecks across the entire stack and work the appropriate teams in Supabase and the wider community to resolve them

What we're looking for

•
Deep experience in performance engineering, specifically performance analysis of complex distributed systems.

•
You can walk the whole stack: follow a tail-latency problem from the query optimizer through the syscall boundary to the IO scheduler — or across pooler hops, network paths, and availability zones — reading profiles and traces at every layer.

•
Depth on at least one end of that stack: Linux kernel internals (virtual memory, scheduling, networking, IO) or database internals (query planning, storage engines, buffer and WAL management)

•
Strong working knowledge of networking and cloud infrastructure performance: TCP behavior under load, network virtualization overhead, and the performance characteristics of AWS primitives (EBS throughput and IOPS, instance network limits, placement groups, cross-AZ latency).

•
Proven ability to turn performance insights into real product and architecture improvements — including getting teams you don't belong to to prioritize and ship the fix.

•
Strong written communication: your problem characterisations are precise, reproducible, and compelling on their own.

•
Pragmatic, tooling-oriented mindset; comfort working across product, infra, and database teams.

What We Offer

Fully Remote

Tech Allowance

•
Annual Off-Sites

Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

•
Flexible Work

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

•
Professional Development

Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

~400 team members

60+ countries

•
20+ languages spoken

•
Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

•
540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

postings.title: Staff Software Engineer (LatAm Only)
postings.descriptionText:
At R2 , we believe that small and medium businesses are the productive engine of society. Small and medium businesses (SMBs) make up over 90% of companies in Latin America, yet they face a trillion-dollar credit gap. Our mission is to unlock SMBs’ potential by providing financial solutions tailored to their needs. We are reimagining the financial infrastructure of Latin America, where SMBs’ financial needs are met without ever having to go to a bank.
R2 enables platforms across Latin America to embed financial services that SMBs can leverage, starting with revenue-based financing. We are a high-performing, close-knit team with talent from organizations such as Google, Amazon, Nubank, Uber, Capital One, Mercado Libre, Globant, and J.P. Morgan.
We are entering a new phase of growth following a strategic investment from Ant International, focused on rapidly expanding our partner footprint, strengthening our credit and underwriting capabilities, and scaling operations across multiple markets. As part of this growth journey, eligible team members have the opportunity to participate in R2 ’s Phantom Share Program, a performance-based incentive designed to align our team with the company’s long-term success and value creation. We believe in building a culture of ownership, where those who help create value share meaningfully in it.
We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer (IC4) to set technical direction across our core platform. It's a hands-on, high-leverage role for someone who thrives on scope and ambiguity; you'll operate across team boundaries, raise the engineering bar for everyone around you, and stay close enough to the code to build the hardest parts yourself.

What You'll Do

• Partner directly with the Head of Platform Engineering to shape and execute these critical, company-defining projects, translating strategy into architecture and shipped systems.

• Own product and solution architecture across multiple services and teams, not just your own surface area.

• Design, build, and maintain APIs, services, and systems (REST and/or gRPC) that are scalable, observable, and safe to operate.

• Set company-wide standards for reliability, code quality, and engineering practice — and get teams to actually adopt them.

• Drive a "you build it, you own it" culture: services shipped with the metrics, tracing, dashboards, SLOs, and alerting needed to be owned end-to-end by the team that builds them.

• Champion trunk-based development, feature flags, and safe, incremental delivery as the default way we ship.

• Lead large refactors that pay down structural debt without disrupting delivery, and mentor engineers on doing the same.

• Research and invest in tooling that makes the whole engineering org more productive (with a focus on the AI space).

• Ensure delivery of mission-critical systems under tight deadlines and push relentlessly toward a zero-bug bar.

• Think about security throughout everything you do.

• Grow the engineers around you — fostering learning, risk-taking, and accountability, and multiplying your impact through others.

Who You Are

• 8+ years of engineering experience building API-driven services, with the appetite and ability to code on a daily basis.

• Deep expertise designing and constructing web services in REST and/or gRPC, from interface design through production operation.

• Strong track record with distributed architecture patterns, in particular microservices and monolith decomposition — you've done this at real scale, not just on a whiteboard.

• Hands-on experience designing and implementing event-driven architectures.

• Experience with change data capture (CDC) — streaming changes out of operational databases (e.g., Postgres WAL / logical replication, Debezium, or equivalent) to power replication, event pipelines, and downstream analytics.

• High proficiency with observability across all three pillars — traces, metrics, and logs. Deep hands-on experience with OpenTelemetry for instrumentation, and with metrics systems (Prometheus and PromQL, or equivalent) for defining SLIs, dashboards, and alerting — and using that telemetry to actually drive decisions.

• Solid, demonstrable refactoring ability: you can restructure large, load-bearing codebases safely and incrementally.

• Fluent with trunk-based development, feature flags, and continuous, low-risk delivery.

• Strong proficiency in Go (required). Additional experience with Java, Python, or Rust is a plus.

• Experience designing and implementing robust production data models using databases like PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, and/or Snowflake — including data lifecycle, retention, and archival concerns.

• Solid grasp of the OLTP–OLAP divide — designing transactional systems for low-latency operational workloads while feeding analytical stores (e.g. Snowflake) for reporting and analytics, and knowing where each belongs.

• Experience with containers (Docker, Docker Compose, Kubernetes).

• Hands-on experience designing and operating full-text search (e.g. Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, or PostgreSQL full-text search) in production — indexing, relevance, and query performance at scale.

• Professional working proficiency in both English and Spanish (required) — you'll collaborate across teams and markets in both languages daily.

• The judgment and communication skills to influence technical direction across teams and align engineers and stakeholders around a shared plan.

Bonus Points

• Prior experience in fintech, banking, payments, or lending — especially in regulated, high-reliability environments where correctness and auditability are non-negotiable.

• Experience building systems that move money: payments, ledgers, settlement, reconciliation, or double-entry accounting, with a healthy respect for idempotency, exactly-once semantics, and consistency guarantees.

• Familiarity with financial-grade correctness concerns — handling money without floating point, transaction integrity, immutability, and building for auditability from day one.

• Experience integrating with third-party financial rails and partners: banks, acquirers, card networks, payment processors, or KYC/identity providers.

• Exposure to fraud, risk, or credit-decisioning systems, and the real-time data pipelines that feed them.

• Understanding of financial regulatory and compliance concerns (PCI DSS, SOC 2, data residency, PII handling) and how they shape system design.

• Experience operating high-availability, low-latency systems where downtime has direct financial and trust consequences, and designing for graceful degradation and disaster recovery.

• Experience with cold storage / tiered storage architectures and data-lifecycle management at scale.

• Familiarity with agent/LLM infrastructure, MCP, policy engines (e.g., OPA/Rego), event streaming, and vector stores.

• Portuguese proficiency, a plus as we expand into Brazil.

What We Offer

• The chance to join a high-impact, mission-driven fintech.

• Ownership and impact in a fast-paced, growth-oriented startup.

• Cross-functional collaboration with exceptional teams across Latin America and Europe.

• Exposure to complex regulatory challenges and innovation in embedded finance.

Location: São Paulo, Buenos Aires or Santiago.

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato .

YOUR ROLE
You'll build the models that decide which carrier each auto insurance shopper sees on our click wall. The goal is to send every user to the carrier most likely to convert them, so carriers see our traffic convert and raise their bids. You'll also own the buying models behind our media spend, which are held to ROAS.
Carrier conversion data (quotes, policies and acquisition cost) is now coming back to us, and you'll be the one who puts it to work in production. The hard part is the data. Outcomes land weeks or months after the click, many sessions are sparse, the same shoppers come back, and the market drifts. Our bids also decide which users we win, so the model shapes the data it learns from next.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You frame problems directly with the business, find your own data, build and validate the model, and stay with it through deployment and monitoring. An ML engineer works alongside you on the production side. Auto insurance takes most of your time to start, and scope broadens to other verticals over time.
We're remote first, and most of the company works East Coast hours.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
By day 60, you run our insurance marketplace media buying on your own.

By the end of your first year:

• Click wall serving that matches each user to the right carrier

• Carrier conversion data running in production models

• Automated marketplace bidding taken from proof of concept to scale

• A clear approach for repeat users and sparse sessions

• Production models that hold up through drift and changing objectives

• Output the business trusts and uses without rework

• 5+ years of hands-on applied data science with measurable business impact

• Your models drove paid media decisions: spend, bidding or ad serving. Attribution and reporting alone don't qualify.

• You built what's on your resume and can explain it down to the loss function and architecture choice, neural network fundamentals included

• You see how today's bids shape tomorrow's training data, and you've handled late labels, sparse features or drift

• You own models end to end: you find your own data, build through deployment and monitoring, and bring a point of view

• Expert Python and SQL

NICE TO HAVES

• Real ad budget spent in live auctions

• Large-scale ranking or recommendation systems

• Explaining tradeoffs to non-technical partners in plain terms

• Designing for auction feedback loops, selection bias and exploration

• Hands-on neural network work, such as embeddings of text, creative or user behavior

• AWS for data science: ECS, S3, Athena, SageMaker

• CI/CD deployment

HR Manager

Full-Time, Remote (Europe)

About Prism Studio

Prism Studio is a Malta-based, independent video game development company focused on building unforgettable, player-first experiences driven by clear artistic direction, state-of-the-art tools and a strong visual identity. Our work is guided by a culture of innovation, creativity and close collaboration, allowing us to pursue our vision of bringing back the fun in video games and creating experiences that feel engaging, rewarding and memorable for players. We operate as a fully remote studio with a globally distributed team of experienced developers, artists and designers. Prism is structured around trust, accountability and clear communication, enabling us to collaborate efficiently across time zones while maintaining a consistent standard of quality and execution.
The studio is currently developing its first PvPvE multiplayer showdown shooter, Heptic Arena, with the aim of standing out within the genre and leaving a lasting impression on players. Join us on our exciting journey as we continue to build cutting-edge games, push the boundaries of what’s possible in the gaming world, and provide unparalleled entertainment and compelling experiences for players around the globe!

Why This Role Matters
At Prism, our people directly shape the quality of the games we build. As a growing independent studio, having the right people in the right roles, and giving them the environment, structure and support to do their best work, is critical to our success.
The HR Manager will take ownership of the people function across the studio, combining strategic workforce planning with hands-on recruitment, employee relations and HR operations. You will work closely with the CEO, studio leadership and hiring managers to anticipate talent needs, strengthen our people processes and ensure Prism continues to grow without losing the culture and ways of working that make the studio effective.
This is not a role focused solely on policies or administration. You will be expected to understand how the studio operates, recognise where people-related challenges could affect production and take action before they become larger problems. Whether that means identifying a future hiring need, improving onboarding, supporting a manager through a difficult conversation or spotting early signs of disengagement, you will play an important role in keeping the team healthy, productive and aligned.
Just as importantly, you will help create an environment where people feel comfortable raising concerns, giving honest feedback and taking ownership of problems. We want HR to be trusted, practical and embedded in the studio, not something people only interact with when there is a problem.

What You’ll Do

Talent Acquisition & Workforce Planning

• Own full-cycle recruitment across the studio, from workforce planning and role scoping through sourcing, interviewing, offer negotiation and hiring.

• Partner closely with the CEO, department leads and hiring managers to anticipate future talent needs and identify capability gaps before they begin affecting production.

• Recruit across technical, creative and operational disciplines, with a strong understanding of how to engage experienced professionals within the games and technology industries.

• Translate business and production requirements into clear, compelling job descriptions that accurately communicate the role, expectations and Prism’s culture.

• Build and maintain strong candidate pipelines for current and future hiring needs, ensuring candidates receive clear communication and timely feedback throughout the process.

• Design structured and consistent hiring processes, including interview stages, technical or creative assessments, evaluation criteria and scorecards.

• Lead offer development and negotiations, balancing candidate expectations, internal consistency, market conditions and company budgets.

• Continuously improve our ATS, recruitment workflows, candidate experience and hiring metrics.

Compensation & Market Intelligence

• Maintain a strong understanding of compensation trends across the games and technology sectors, particularly within European markets.

• Conduct salary benchmarking and provide informed recommendations when defining compensation ranges for new and existing roles.

• Develop competitive and sustainable offers that balance market expectations, internal equity and Prism’s financial objectives.

• Support leadership with workforce cost planning, payroll forecasting and people-related budgeting.

Employee Experience & HR Operations

• Own the employee lifecycle from onboarding through development, retention and off-boarding.

• Build an onboarding experience that gives new hires the tools, access, context and relationships they need to integrate quickly and contribute effectively.

• Manage core HR operations including employment contracts, employee records, payroll coordination, benefits, leave and absence management, HR systems and documentation.

• Maintain accurate, organised and compliant HR records and processes across the studio.

• Continuously review HR workflows and identify opportunities to simplify, automate or improve how we work.

Employee Relations & People Support

• Act as a trusted and approachable HR partner for employees and managers across the studio.

• Provide a neutral and confidential point of contact for workplace concerns, interpersonal challenges and difficult conversations.

• Identify potential issues early and work with the people involved to reach practical, constructive solutions before problems escalate.

• Support managers in handling performance concerns, feedback, conflict and other people-related situations confidently and consistently.

• Recognise unhealthy team dynamics and help individuals and managers move toward accountability, direct communication and effective problem-solving.

• Manage disciplinary matters and terminations professionally, fairly and in accordance with applicable employment law and company policy, ensuring documentation and communication are handled appropriately.

• Monitor indicators such as engagement, absence, workload and turnover to identify potential retention or employee-experience concerns early.

Culture, Engagement & Leadership Partnership

• Work closely with the CEO and leadership team to continue shaping Prism’s culture, values and ways of working as the studio grows.

• Be a key contributor to initiatives that improve the employee experience, working environment and overall health of the organisation.

• Partner with the wider HR team on initiatives relating to engagement, well-being, inclusion and psychological safety.

• Develop meaningful remote-first initiatives, events and team rituals that strengthen connection across a distributed workforce.

• Coach and support managers on interviewing, people management, HR policies, internal tools and effective communication.

• Use employee feedback and HR data to identify opportunities for improvement and turn those insights into practical action.

About You

• 5+ years of progressive HR experience, ideally including experience within a medium-to-large technology, gaming or similarly fast-paced organisation.

• Knowledge of Maltese employment law and/or experience employing and hiring people across multiple EU jurisdictions.

• Strong full-cycle recruitment experience across technical and/or creative roles within the technology or gaming industries.

• Proven experience designing and running structured hiring processes that balance speed with rigorous candidate assessment.

• Strong experience managing candidate pipelines and proactively sourcing hard-to-find talent.

• Hands-on experience with salary benchmarking, compensation planning, offer development and negotiation.

• Broad HR experience beyond recruitment, including areas such as onboarding, employee relations, HR operations, performance management and off-boarding.

• Comfortable handling sensitive employee matters, workplace conflict and difficult conversations with professionalism, neutrality and sound judgement.

• Strong understanding of team dynamics and the ability to identify people-related risks before they escalate.

• Experience partnering directly with senior leadership on culture, organisational development and improvements to the working environment.

• Comfortable taking ownership of HR initiatives from identifying a problem through to designing and implementing the solution.

• Highly organised, autonomous and able to prioritise effectively within a fast-moving environment.

• Approachable and trustworthy, with strong judgement around confidentiality, escalation and sensitive information.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with fluency in English.

• Confident working with the Atlassian ecosystem, particularly Jira and Confluence, including the ability to understand Jira projects, workflows and reporting.

• Experienced working within a Slack-based communication culture and comfortable establishing or reinforcing clear communication protocols in a remote environment.

• Comfortable using AI tools as part of your day-to-day work and curious about how automation and emerging technology can improve HR workflows, recruitment and internal processes.

• Genuine interest in games, game development and the people who build them, with an understanding that passion for the player experience starts with the team behind it.

Nice to Have

• Experience working within a fully remote, multinational organisation.

• Previous experience working directly within a game development studio.

• Training or certification in coaching, mediation, conflict resolution or a related discipline.

• Experience using HR analytics to understand areas such as engagement, retention, attrition, absence and workforce trends.

• Experience building or scaling HR processes within a growing organisation.

• An active interest in gaming, particularly multiplayer, competitive or shooter titles.

Life at Prism Studio

We work as one unit with one common goal. Our purpose is to build a cross-disciplinary team where everyone is self-managing, wherever they are in the world. We collaborate in an open, friendly way, as a global team built on talent and communication.

postings.title: Staff Data Scientist, Lead Generation
postings.descriptionText:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato .

YOUR ROLE
You'll build the models that decide which carrier each auto insurance shopper sees on our click wall. The goal is to send every user to the carrier most likely to convert them, so carriers see our traffic convert and raise their bids. You'll also own the buying models behind our media spend, which are held to ROAS.
Carrier conversion data (quotes, policies and acquisition cost) is now coming back to us, and you'll be the one who puts it to work in production. The hard part is the data. Outcomes land weeks or months after the click, many sessions are sparse, the same shoppers come back, and the market drifts. Our bids also decide which users we win, so the model shapes the data it learns from next.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You frame problems directly with the business, find your own data, build and validate the model, and stay with it through deployment and monitoring. An ML engineer works alongside you on the production side. Auto insurance takes most of your time to start, and scope broadens to other verticals over time.
We're remote first, and most of the company works East Coast hours.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
By day 60, you run our insurance marketplace media buying on your own.

By the end of your first year:

• Click wall serving that matches each user to the right carrier

• Carrier conversion data running in production models

• Automated marketplace bidding taken from proof of concept to scale

• A clear approach for repeat users and sparse sessions

• Production models that hold up through drift and changing objectives

• Output the business trusts and uses without rework

MUST HAVE

• 5+ years of hands-on applied data science with measurable business impact

• Your models drove paid media decisions: spend, bidding or ad serving. Attribution and reporting alone don't qualify.

• You built what's on your resume and can explain it down to the loss function and architecture choice, neural network fundamentals included

• You see how today's bids shape tomorrow's training data, and you've handled late labels, sparse features or drift

• You own models end to end: you find your own data, build through deployment and monitoring, and bring a point of view

• Expert Python and SQL

NICE TO HAVES

• Real ad budget spent in live auctions

• Large-scale ranking or recommendation systems

• Explaining tradeoffs to non-technical partners in plain terms

• Designing for auction feedback loops, selection bias and exploration

• Hands-on neural network work, such as embeddings of text, creative or user behavior

• AWS for data science: ECS, S3, Athena, SageMaker

• CI/CD deployment

Want to accelerate your career? Apply now!

Since day one, we've been committed to having a diverse, inclusive team and culture. We are proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity company. We value diversity, equity, and inclusion.

We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

postings.title: Portfolio Manager - Middle Market Underwriting Specialist (LatAm Only)
postings.descriptionText:
At R2 , we believe that small and medium businesses are the productive engine of society. Small and medium businesses (SMBs) make up over 90% of companies in Latin America, yet they face a trillion-dollar credit gap. Our mission is to unlock SMBs’ potential by providing financial solutions tailored to their needs. We are reimagining the financial infrastructure of Latin America, where SMBs’ financial needs are met without ever having to go to a bank.
R2 enables platforms across Latin America to embed financial services that SMBs can leverage, starting with revenue-based financing. We are a high-performing, close-knit team with talent from organizations such as Google, Amazon, Nubank, Uber, Capital One, Mercado Libre, Globant, and J.P. Morgan.
We are entering a new phase of growth following a strategic investment from Ant International, focused on rapidly expanding our partner footprint, strengthening our credit and underwriting capabilities, and scaling operations across multiple markets. As part of this growth journey, eligible team members have the opportunity to participate in R2 ’s Phantom Share Program, a performance-based incentive designed to align our team with the company’s long-term success and value creation. We believe in building a culture of ownership, where those who help create value share meaningfully in it.
R2 ’s Credit Risk team is hiring a Portfolio Manager - Middle Market Underwriting Specialist to own the day-to-day credit execution across our Middle Market and Long Tail portfolios. In Middle Market, you will review large financing applications end to end and make the credit decision. In Long Tail, you will handle individual exceptions and, as you gain independence, contribute to policy. You will also run the team’s weekly and monthly portfolio monitoring and validate the monthly offer batches across our partners.

What you’ll do

• Review Large Loans applications end to end using transactional, credit bureau, financial, and tax data. Approve, reject or counter-offer, and present this in a committee

• Handle credit exceptions and counter-offers across Large Loans and Long Tail: analyze the request, decide or escalate, and follow through until the merchant has an answer. Own the underwriting pipeline for Large Loans

• Support the Product Manager and Commercial on merchant cases raised by partners, and provide the credit answer.

• Own the weekly and monthly monitoring of the Large Loans portfolio: originations, early delinquency, roll rates, NPL and concentration by partner, country and merchant.

• Follow large exposures after disbursement and catch early warning signs, such as falling sales, payment delays or bureau changes, so we can act before they turn into losses.

• Validate each partner’s monthly offer batch before it goes out, and flag anything that looks off.

• Present status of the portfolio in a Credit committee with KPIs and targets.

• Analyze segment performance by cohort, partner, ticket size, industry and risk profile to understand what drives losses and what drives good performance.

• Detect patterns that improve the risk-return of the segment: rules that generate false positives, profiles where we can grow safely, and signals that predict default earlier.

• Turn what you find into concrete policy proposals and bring them to the team’s portfolio and credit strategy reviews.

• Run your analysis with AI tools while directing the work yourself: decide what to look at, check the output against the data, and own the conclusion.

Who You Are

• +2 years in credit analysis, underwriting or credit risk at a fintech, bank or lender.

• Experience reading credit bureau reports, financial statements or tax documentation.

• Comfortable with portfolio metrics: delinquency, roll rates, cohort/vintage analysis and loss rates.

• Intermediate SQL and basic Python: enough to build your own monitoring queries and to read and check the code an AI tool writes for you, not just run it.

• Fluent written and spoken English.

• Judgment under a defined risk appetite: you form a view, decide and write down why.

• Curiosity about the numbers: when a metric moves, you want to know why.

• Organized and reliable with recurring processes and service levels.

Bonus

• Experience in revenue-based financing, embedded lending or merchant cash advance.

• Knowledge of credit bureau reports and SII tax documentation.

• Knowledge of the Latin American payments or acquiring market.

• Experience building dashboards (e.g. Tableau).

• Spanish or Portuguese.

What We Offer

• The chance to join a high-impact, mission-driven fintech.

• Ownership and impact in a fast-paced, growth-oriented startup.

• Cross-functional collaboration with exceptional teams.

• Exposure to complex regulatory challenges and innovation in embedded finance.

Locations: Buenos Aires, São Paulo, Bogotá, Santiago

Saphetor ’s mission is to enable anyone to find, share and use the most comprehensive human genome data – and to collaborate to improve health and lives around the world. Strongly Valued

• Platform Experience: Previous background managing API gateways such as APISIX, and building or maintaining CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Workflows or Cloud Build.

• Monitoring Knowledge: Familiarity with logging and monitoring tools such as Elasticsearch, Kibana, Grafana, or cloud-native solutions.

• Certifications: GCP or OCI certifications are nice to have.

• Global Mindset: Proven experience in multicultural environments and/or supporting internationally distributed engineering teams in a scale-up setting.

Mindset & Key Skills

• Technical Rigor: A curious, detail-oriented professional who maintains high engineering standards while managing complex infrastructure.

• Continuous Improvement Mindset: A proactive mindset with a passion for continuous improvement and learning new technologies, balancing system reliability with pragmatic delivery decisions and translating infrastructure improvements into team and business benefits.

• Self-Organization: A structured thinker with strong prioritization and project management skills, comfortable in a fast-paced environment.

• Agile Collaboration: Comfortable working within Agile frameworks, including Scrumban, as part of a regionally distributed team.

While our foundation is in Athens, our talent pool is spread across Europe, with a strong culture of remote collaboration. Our team is highly experienced in distributed Agile workflows and communicates exclusively in fluent English.

• A position in a fascinating healthcare growth domain, at the cutting edge of technology and research

• A remote-first work environment that promotes a healthy work-life balance, giving you the autonomy to thrive from anywhere.

postings.title: RevOps Engineer
