postings.descriptionText:
About Carrot :

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com .

The Opportunity

Carrot is looking for a Fertility Medical Expert (RN, NP, or PA) to join our Medical Experts team on a contract basis for approximately a 3-month engagement, working a minimum 15 hours per week in a fully remote role. In this role, you will serve as a clinical resource for members navigating fertility and family-building, providing evidence-informed information and guidance that helps people understand their options and make confident, informed choices.

Day to day, you will meet with members by video to talk through their fertility questions and goals, offering clear, practical information without diagnosing, prescribing, or directing care..

This is a chance to put your fertility experience to work in a fast-growing digital health environment, with the flexibility of a contract schedule. You will work alongside a diverse team of medical experts across fertility, pregnancy, urology, mental health, and nutrition who share a passion for continuous learning and an evidence-based approach.

What You’ll Own

In this role, you will:

• Provide members with evidence-informed information and guidance on fertility topics, such as fertility evaluation and testing, treatment options, and family-building pathways

• Conduct one-on-one virtual sessions (video) that educate and present options without diagnosing, prescribing, or directing care

• Stay current on reproductive and fertility regulatory trends and clinical practice guidelines in the US

• Participate in quality assurance initiatives and audits to help ensure a safe, compliant member experience that meets the highest standards

• Collaborate with the broader Medical Experts team and cross-functional partners to deliver a consistent, high-quality member experience

• Maintain a reliable, flexible schedule within ~15 hours per week range to meet member demand throughout the engagement

What Success Looks Like

In your first 30 Days, you will have:

• Delivered consistently high-quality, well-rated fertility sessions that help members feel informed and supported

• Stayed within Carrot’s non-diagnostic, non-directive scope of practice and met documentation and quality standards across member interactions

• Met your agreed weekly hours and availability, communicating proactively about scheduling and capacity

• Ramped up quickly and worked independently with minimal oversight in a confidential, remote environment

• Built trusted working relationships with the Medical Experts team and cross-functional partners

About You ✨

You likely have:

• An active US license as a Registered Nurse (RN), Nurse Practitioner (NP), or Physician Assistant (PA)

• 3+ years of experience providing patient care in a fertility clinic or a hospital clinic that addresses reproductive health

• Superb listening skills and the ability to empathetically discuss fertility and family-building topics

• The ability to work independently and to distinguish good clinical judgment from non-directive guidance

• The ability to work from a confidential and private remote environment with reliable internet and digital resources

• Flexibility to adapt to evolving business needs and availability for 15 per week for a 3-month engagement

Nice to Have ⭐

While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring:

• Experience in third-party reproduction (e.g., gestational surrogacy, donor gametes), urology, pregnancy, or menopause

• Experience in digital health or telehealth settings, including virtual member or patient education

• Prior contract or consulting experience with a quick ramp-up

• Fluency in an additional language

Why This Role Matters

Fertility journeys are deeply personal, and members often arrive with more questions than answers. As a Fertility Medical Expert, you will be the knowledgeable, compassionate clinical voice who helps them understand their options and feel prepared for the conversations they have with their own care teams.

Your expertise helps make Carrot’s clinical program one that members trust and rely on, and it strengthens the confidence of the employers and health plans who count on Carrot to deliver high-quality, whole-person care. Even in a focused 3-month engagement, your work will make a direct, visible difference for the people we serve.

Interview Process

We believe in a thoughtful and transparent interview process designed to create alignment for both candidates and our team.

For this role, candidates can expect:

• Recruiter Screen — 30 minutes

• Hiring Manager Interview — 30–45 minutes

• Mock Chat- 45 Minutes

Throughout the process, we will share additional context about the team, business priorities, customer landscape, and what success looks like in this role.

Why Candidates Join Carrot

Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission.

Highlights include:

• A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally.

• A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact.

• Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits.

• Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge.

• Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits.

• A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture.

• The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide.

Compensation

The starting base hourly for this position will range from $70-$90/hr. Actual compensation may vary from posted base salary depending on your confirmed job-related skills and experience.

Fraud and Security Notice: Please note that all communication regarding job opportunities at Carrot will come exclusively from an @get-carrot.com email address. If you receive messages from any other domain, please disregard them and report the incident to: securityreporting@get-carrot.com

A Note on AI

At Carrot, we believe AI can help us work smarter, move faster, and create more meaningful experiences for our members, customers, and each other. While not every role requires deep technical AI expertise, we value people who are curious, eager to learn, and excited to thoughtfully incorporate AI into their day-to-day work.

For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement—and we'll call that out clearly in the qualifications. For everyone else, we're looking for people who embrace new ways of working, use AI responsibly to improve quality and efficiency, and continue to learn as the technology evolves.

Why Carrot?

Carrot has received national and international recognition for its pioneering work, including Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and World Changing Ideas, Inc. Power Partners, and Modern Healthcare’s Innovators. Carrot’s global workforce has been acknowledged with several accolades, including Fortune’s Best Workplaces in Healthcare, Great Place to Work, and Age-Friendly Employer certifications. Carrot is regularly featured in media reporting on issues related to the future of work, women in leadership, and healthcare innovation, including MSNBC, The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, CNBC, National Public Radio, Harvard Business Review, and more. Learn more at carrotfertility.com.

postings.descriptionText:
About Command|Link
Command|Link is a global SaaS Platform providing network, voice services, and IT security solutions, helping corporations consolidate their core infrastructure into a single vendor and layering on a proprietary single pane of glass platform. Command|Link has revolutionized the IT industry by tackling the problems our competitors create. In recognition for our unprecedented innovation and dedication, Command|Link was recognized as the SD-WAN Product of the Year, ITSM Visionary Spotlight, UCaaS Product of the Year, NaaS Product of the Year, Supplier of the Year, and the AT&T Strategic Growth Partner. Command|Link has built the only IT platform for scale that solves ISP vendor sprawl and IT headaches. We make it easy for our customers to get more done, maximize uptime and improve the bottom line.
Learn more about us here!
This is a 100% remote position
About your new role:
CommandLink 's monitoring product is how customers see their network: every device, service, and dependency, surfaced through an API and UI they use every day. Today that experience is harder to build well than it looks, most platforms in this space bury the signal in flat device lists and dated interfaces. We want to build something clearer and faster, grounded in real network topology instead.
As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll own that surface end to end: the architecture that determines how it scales, how it consumes the classification and telemetry layers beneath it, and how it evolves as the platform grows. This is full-stack work with a strong network domain emphasis. You'll need to reason clearly about both system design and the experience it produces for someone troubleshooting their network in real time.
Key Responsibilities:

• Own the architecture and long-term direction of the monitoring product's API and UI, including the roadmap for how it scales and evolves.

• Surface the full account and device hierarchy, from company down through site, probe and collector, device, and service, along with the dependency relationships between them, in a way that stays navigable at scale.

• Lead the discovery and inventory experience: how new devices and hosts are found and billed (Host Discovery), how correlated system summaries are built (System Discovery), and how customers onboard new sources.

• Build the screens customers use to create, edit, and review alert history through the alert service.

• Define the data contracts between the monitoring product and the classification, telemetry, and alert services it depends on, and hold the line on their quality as the platform grows.

• Set the technical patterns other engineers follow for rendering and interacting with complex, hierarchical network data, including topology visualizations that are genuinely performant, a known weak point across competing platforms.

• Dive into other teams' projects when architecture, performance, or design decisions need your judgment, and resolve cross-team dependencies before they become blockers.

• Mentor engineers across the team and raise the bar for what production-grade, domain-aware full-stack work looks like at CommandLink .

• Takes on additional responsibilities and projects as needed to support the success of the team and organization.

What you'll need for success:
Required

• Deep understanding of network and system topology: how devices, services, and infrastructure relate to each other, and how to represent those relationships clearly to someone troubleshooting live.

• Production experience with high-volume, latency-sensitive infrastructure: distributed messaging/event streaming (e.g. Kafka) and search or indexing at scale (e.g. OpenSearch), or clear equivalents.

• Comfort with contract-driven development across teams, using schema/interface definitions like protobuf to keep multiple services honest to a shared contract.

• Working knowledge of how network telemetry looks in production (SNMP, syslog, ICMP, OpenTelemetry, or similar) and the judgment to reason about what a given signal means for a real network environment.

• Strong cloud and systems experience across at least two of AWS, Azure, or GCP.

• A track record of owning architectural decisions in ambiguous problem spaces and driving them to durable outcomes, including influencing shared contracts or platform boundaries across teams.

Nice to Have

• Prior experience building monitoring, observability, or network management products with a customer-facing UI.

• Familiarity with graph data models and how hierarchical or dependency topology is represented and traversed.

• Experience designing data visualizations for complex, hierarchical, or graph-structured data.

• Background with platforms like SolarWinds, Zabbix, PRTG, Auvik, or similar. Understanding what they get right and wrong is the useful part, not having built the better version already.

If you don't check every box here but this sounds like your kind of problem, apply. We're more interested in how you think about this space than a perfect skills match.

postings.title: Field Marketer
postings.descriptionText:
We’re building something ambitious at Fly .io: a new public cloud, running on our own hardware all over the world, built to make it easy to run apps close to users anywhere in the world.
Unlike the vast majority of our roles, this role is geographically specific; field marketing here is in large part about engaging local communities. We’re currently hiring a field marketer who can deliver work full time in North America and Europe, where our Developer Relations Engineers are located.
So far, we’ve focused a lot on self-serve growth: developers (our users) can find us, sign up, and build things on their own. Now, we want to meet developers where they are, out in the world. We’re looking for a Senior Field Marketing Manager to drive our presence in ecosystem events and Developer Relations.
This role combines event management, strategic planning, budget control, and audience engagement. You’ll manage field marketing events from conception through execution, making sure that Fly .io is showing up in an impactful way that’s aligned with who we are as a company. You’ll need to provide calm leadership in high-pressure situations and make sure that events run smoothly, even when challenges (inevitably) occur.
If you’re a community builder, this role should feel magical. Fly .io’s a group of really fun, genuine people, and we need you to help us reach more people like us. We don’t want you to shill; we want you to gameplan how to create over-the-top fun for developers, and then engage with them—using beautiful swag, good conversation, and great food and drinks—so that they become evangelists.
This role will be a good fit for you if:

• You’ve done field marketing, event management, or something similar. (We want you to be able to show us the ropes on Day One.)

• You’re super organized (no details gets past you) and great at project management.

• You can translate Fly .io’s company goals into marketing strategies that resonate with technical audiences.

• You like managing a budget, and know how to get the most “bang for your buck” when it comes to event planning.

• You like to travel. We want to show up in person, all over the US and EU. (You can work from anywhere in North America or Europe, but we expect most of the events you’ll attend will be US/EU!)

• You’re good at remaining poised and effective under stress. You can manage a crisis without disrupting an event or letting the audience know there’s an issue.

• You’re good at managing expectations and pushing back when necessary. We need to keep initiatives on-brand and within budget, even when our internal stakeholders get excited.

• You find it easy to build and sustain relationships, in any medium: in person, over Slack, over email, etc. Do folks call you a “people person?” If so, let’s talk.

You’ll know you’re succeeding in your job if:

•
Fly .io’s culture and public persona is consistent across all our field marketing activities.

• You’re managing the field marketing budget so well that we’re getting far more valuable events than we thought were possible out of it.

• Your field marketing strategy is enhancing Fly .io’s visibility and engagement within the developer community.

• You’re planning and managing all aspects of our events, including logistics, vendor relationships, and on-site coordination.

• You’ve built strong relationships with internal stakeholders, our ecosystem partners, and the broader developer community.

More Details
This is a mid-senior level, full-time salaried position. You can live anywhere in the North America or Europe. In order to optimize for pay equity, Fly .iodoesn’t negotiate salaries. We have standardized salaries for each employee level. The salary for this role is $134k-190k USD. We offer competitive equity grants with a long exercise window. US employees get health care, everyone gets flexible vacation time (with a minimum), hardware/phone allowances, the standard stuff.
We’re weird about hiring. We’re skeptical of resumes and we don’t trust traditional interviews. We respect career experience but we’re more excited about potential.
The premise of our hiring process is that we’re going to give you three challenges, a “work sample”, a “written challenge”, and a “work day”, that each simulate the kind of work you’ll actually be doing here. Unlike a lot of places that assign “take-home problems”, our challenges are the backbone of our whole process; they’re not pre-screeners for an interview gauntlet.
If you’re interested, . You can tell us a bit about yourself, if you like. Please also include 1. your location and 2. your favorite industry euphemism for “customer”, so we know you’re not a bot.

postings.title: Senior Analytics Engineer
postings.descriptionText:
About Imagine Worldwide

All children have immense potential, but hundreds of millions don’t have access to the learning they need. Imagine Worldwide believes that every child should be empowered with the basic right to literacy and numeracy. We provide an innovative education technology solution and implementation model to the global literacy/numeracy learning crisis using the onebillion application and various toolkits and systems to support implementation. Our model is massively scalable, evidence-based, and can deliver foundational learning to millions of the most marginalized children.
Imagine Worldwide partners with governments, organizations, and communities to provide child-directed, tablet-based learning that is accessible, effective, and affordable. We are incorporated in California (United States) as a nonprofit organization, but operate in Sub-Saharan Africa through locally-registered entities in Malawi, Sierra Leone, and Tanzania. Learn more on our website.

Role Overview
The Senior Analytics Engineer builds, runs and improves Imagine’s analytics platform: the infrastructure, pipelines and core data models that the organisation’s reporting and analysis depend on. The central task is to scale the platform as data volumes grow, keeping costs under control without giving up performance. In a small team, that means covering the infrastructure underneath the data as well as the data engineering itself.
Imagine’s data comes from many sources. The largest is tablets in more than 1,500 schools across Malawi, Tanzania and Sierra Leone, which record learning activity as individual events, adding up to billions of records. These only become meaningful when joined with programme context, such as active schools per term, device allocations and enrolment, and with operational data from inventory and field data collection. Turning all of this into reliable data on a non-profit budget calls for careful decisions about where processing happens and what each workload costs.
The role reports to the Director of Analytics, who sets the platform’s architecture and technical standards, and works alongside the rest of the Analytics Team. We are looking for someone senior who takes initiative, turns architectural direction into working systems, and brings forward evidence-based proposals for improving them. As the engineer builds context, they take on increasing ownership of the platform’s day-to-day running and technical decisions.

Key Responsibilities
The Senior Analytics Engineer’s responsibilities fall into four pillars. The first two cover the platform itself: the infrastructure it runs on, and the pipelines that bring data in from many sources and process it at scale. The third covers orchestration and the core data models that the rest of the Analytics Team builds on. The fourth covers the practices that keep the platform reliable, secure and affordable to run.

Data Platform and Infrastructure
Imagine’s analytics platform runs on AWS and ClickHouse Cloud, with infrastructure managed as code. In a small team, this role carries the infrastructure work that a larger organisation would split across dedicated platform or DevOps staff, limited to the scope of the analytics platform.

• Build and maintain the platform’s AWS infrastructure, including storage, compute, networking, the data catalogue, secrets and access management (S3, EC2, Glue Data Catalog, Lake Formation, IAM, Secrets Manager).

• Manage infrastructure as code in Terraform, keeping environments reproducible, version-controlled and reviewable.

• Administer the ClickHouse Cloud warehouse, including service configuration, user and role management, and monitoring of performance and capacity.

• Host and maintain the team’s self-hosted tools, including Apache Superset for BI and Apache Airflow for orchestration. This covers deployment, upgrades, authentication and availability. The Senior BI & Data Analyst manages the dashboards and content within Superset.

• Contribute to architectural decisions on how the platform evolves, setting out options and trade-offs for review with the Director of Analytics.

Large-Scale Data Processing and Pipelines
Data reaches the platform from application databases, operational systems and field data tools, and lands in an Apache Iceberg data lake on S3. Spark-based processing on AWS Glue does the heavy work before the data moves into ClickHouse for analysis. The aim is to do expensive processing once, as far upstream as practical, so that downstream models and queries stay fast and affordable.

• Build and maintain ingestion pipelines from the platform’s sources, including application databases, APIs and operational systems, using tools such as AWS Glue, Airbyte and AWS Lambda.

• Implement incremental loading patterns that stay efficient and recoverable as volumes grow, landing raw data in the lake in a form that preserves its full history.

• Develop and optimise Spark jobs that process billions of device events into learning sessions and higher-level aggregates, paying close attention to partitioning, skew and compute cost.

• Bring in and model the programme context that gives event data its meaning, such as schools, terms, device allocations and enrolment, and handle how that context changes over time.

• Design and maintain Iceberg tables for performance and cost, including partitioning strategy, file sizing, compaction and snapshot management.

• Validate data at ingestion and surface quality issues early, working with the Analytics Team to trace them back to their source.

• Contribute to evaluating new processing approaches as volumes grow, including moving more work upstream and assessing where streaming would add value.

Orchestration and Transformation
Apache Airflow orchestrates the platform’s pipelines, and dbt transforms data in ClickHouse into the models that reporting and analysis rely on. This role builds and maintains the foundational layers of those models.

• Build and maintain Airflow workflows that coordinate ingestion, processing and transformation, with clear dependencies, retries and alerting.

• Develop and maintain dbt staging and core models in ClickHouse, following consistent conventions for naming, structure and materialisation.

• Implement incremental models for high-volume tables, choosing materialisation strategies and table designs that balance freshness, correctness and cost.

• Write and maintain dbt tests and model contracts for core datasets, so that changes that would break downstream reporting are caught before they reach production.

• Document core models such as learning sessions as agreed definitions, including their lineage, and make clear where a model applies an approximation rather than a direct transformation.

• Work with the Senior BI & Data Analyst on the boundary between core and reporting models, and with the Data Scientist on datasets for research and evaluation.

Reliability, Cost and Engineering Practice
A small team needs a platform that runs predictably and that more than one person understands. This pillar covers the engineering practices that make that possible.

• Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines in GitHub Actions for infrastructure, pipeline and dbt code, including automated checks that stop unsafe changes from reaching production.

• Implement monitoring and alerting across pipelines, the warehouse and hosted tools, so that failures and delays are visible quickly and reach the right people.

• Respond to platform incidents and data issues, carry out root cause analysis, and contribute to the team’s data quality incident process.

• Apply and maintain access controls and security practices across the data lake, warehouse and BI layer, in line with Imagine’s data governance policies.

• Monitor platform costs across AWS and ClickHouse, track the cost and performance of individual workloads over time, and use that evidence to identify savings and prioritise optimisation work.

• Maintain and periodically test backup and recovery procedures for the platform’s core components.

• Take part in code review and write clear runbooks and technical documentation, following the team’s documentation standards, so that knowledge of the platform is shared across the team.

Requirements
The qualifications below are grouped by importance. Core requirements are needed to do the role from the start. Strongly preferred skills shorten the time it takes to become effective on Imagine’s platform. Advantageous experience adds value but is not expected. We do not expect any one candidate to bring everything listed here.

Education

• A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Demonstrated experience is weighted equally to formal credentials.

Experience

• At least 7 years in data engineering, software engineering or platform engineering roles, including at least 3 years building and running distributed data processing (Spark or equivalent) in production.

• A track record of taking responsibility for a production data platform, or major parts of one, including its reliability, performance and day-to-day operation.

• Experience working with datasets in the hundreds of millions to billions of records, and designing processing that stays efficient as volumes grow.

• Experience running data workloads within real budget constraints: making deliberate trade-offs between compute, storage and performance, and being able to show the effect of those decisions.

• Experience managing the cloud infrastructure that data workloads run on, not only using managed services.

• Experience in small teams where engineers cover a broad scope and work with limited supervision.

• Experience working with remote teams across multiple countries and time zones.

• Experience in the non-profit, international development or social sector is an advantage but not a requirement.

Technical Skills: Core

• Strong Python, written to production standards, with testing and modular design.

• Advanced SQL, including writing and optimising queries against analytical databases.

• Spark (PySpark), including performance tuning for partitioning, shuffles and data skew.

• A solid understanding of data lake design, including columnar formats such as Parquet, partitioning strategy, and when to process in the lake rather than the warehouse.

• Hands-on AWS experience with data services and the infrastructure around them, such as S3, Glue or EMR, IAM and EC2.

• Infrastructure as code, using Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK or similar.

• Linux administration and Docker, to the level needed to deploy and maintain self-hosted services.

• dbt in production, including incremental models and testing.

• Workflow orchestration with Airflow, Dagster, Prefect or similar.

• Git, CI/CD and code review practice.

Technical Skills: Strongly Preferred

• Apache Iceberg, or another open table format such as Delta Lake or Hudi.

• ClickHouse, or a comparable columnar warehouse such as Snowflake, BigQuery or Redshift.

• Terraform specifically.

• Apache Airflow specifically.

• AWS Glue and Lake Formation.

• Data modelling for analytics, including handling reference data that changes over time.

Technical Skills: Advantageous

• Managed Spark platforms such as Databricks.

• Streaming technologies such as Kafka, Flink, Kinesis or Spark Structured Streaming.

• Event, telemetry or IoT data, particularly from devices that sync intermittently.

• Ingestion tools such as Airbyte.

• Administering BI tools such as Apache Superset.

• Software development beyond data pipelines, such as building APIs or system integrations.

Compensation & Benefits
Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience.

Location
The Senior Analytics Engineer must be based in Africa. The role will frequently collaborate and coordinate with operations teams across Africa, the US, and the UK.

postings.title: Developer Relations Engineer
postings.descriptionText:
We’re Fly .io, and we’re building a new public cloud. We transmogrify containers into lightweight VMs and run them on our hardware around the world – hundreds of thousands of applications rely on us, running on every continent except Antarctica. If you haven’t already,take us for spin. Your app will be up and running in just minutes.
Unlike all the rest of our roles, these roles are geographically specific; devrel here is in large part about engaging local communities. We’re currently hiring devrel people who can deliver work full time in North America and Europe. Of course, our whole thing is that we deploy everywhere else in the world, too, so we’ll be expanding from there soon.
There are a lot DevRel jobs where you have to make your own fun, because the product is about eliminating some gnarly business slog like inventory management or expense tracking or underwriting. We’re not knocking those jobs! There’s nobility in eliminating slogs!
But this isn’t one of those jobs. We’re doing something big, something that’s about software development itself. We’re one of a number of upstart companies rethinking the public cloud, breaking down infrastructure problems that used to take months of work and dedicated headcount into a platform that our users can gain fluency with in a matter of minutes. If you’re our kind of developer, the fun in this job is built-in.
Folks working in DevRel at Fly .io interact with three different groups of people:

• Group A: our product teams, like in every other devrel job: the people building the platform and its features.

• Group B: our “framework” teams, which are a fun quirk of Fly .io: these are small teams of people organized around individual application frameworks like Rails, Django, Phoenix, and whatever people are doing in Javascript these days.

• Group H: the “developer community”, a term the industry uses because it is apparently squicked out by the word “customer”.

You’ll accomplish this by deploying all of your “skills of an artist”, hopefully including things like:

• Quickly building proof-of-concept applications that show off cool things about Fly .io, like how quickly you can start up a new VM, or the timeless elegance of our IPv6 addressing.

• Building and delivering presentations for events, presentations that have the net effect of customers (err, the developer community) liking us more. Also, having the good taste to do this in ways that are interesting even to people who might never deploy an app on Fly .io.

• Talking to people working on all kinds of applications, from side projects to large teams building microservice ensembles, and talking them through making the best use of Fly .io, the Fly Machines API, our integrations with products like Supabase, that sort of stuff.

• Maintaining a public presence in online communities where developers congregate, and somehow doing all of this while maintaining your own authenticity and credibility. We’ll help!

• 25% monthly travel (with seasonal variability) to meet with developer communities in person to engage in small and large settings to build authentic developer interest in various regions and communities.

This Role Is A Good Fit For You If:

• You enjoy building applications and are particularly psyched about the prototyping phase of building things, because there’s going to be a lot of that here.

• The idea of a little bit of chaos appeals to you, because it’s a sign to you that there’s an opportunity to help define a new practice and make some big moves.

• You’re opinionated enough to be interesting, but exceptionally good at listening, empathizing, and rolling with the opinions of our users. That’s a hard tradeoff and not a lot of us here can do it!

• Your career goals involve increasing your public profile. We punch above our weight in getting attention from developers, and your job here would be part of building and expanding on that.

• Going to a bunch of different developer events sounds like a good time to you. There’s some travel involved in this job.

You’ll Know You’re Succeeding If:

• The numbers are going up and to the right (or you’ve built a time machine and can make the numbers go left).

• You’re involved in helping systematize our content development past blog posts and documentation and into a library of different kinds of content to connect with people at different phases of their use of the product, and you’re seeing results.

• You’re comfortable with how Fly .io intersects with all the major app frameworks and can effectively talk people through solving problems, and when you do that, the result is that people are excited to use us.

More Details
This is a fully-remote, full-time position.
In order to optimize for pay equity, Fly .io doesn’t negotiate salaries. We have standardized salaries for each employee level. The salary for this role is, depending on level, $134k or $190k USD. We offer competitive equity grants with a long exercise window. US employees get health care, everyone gets flexible vacation time (with a minimum), hardware/phone allowances, the standard stuff.
Our hiring process may be a little different from what you’re used to. We respect career experience but we aren’t hypnotized by it, and we’re thrilled at the prospect of discovering new talent. So instead of resumes and interviews, we’re going to show you the kind of work we’re doing and then see if you enjoy actually doing it, with “work-sample challenges”. Unlike a lot of places that assign “take-home problems”, our challenges are the backbone of our whole process; they’re not pre-screeners for an interview gauntlet. (We’re happy to talk, though!)
If you’re interested, mail . You can tell us a bit about yourself, if you like. Please also include 1. your location and 2. your favorite industry euphemism for “customer”, so we know you’re not a bot.

📣 What you’ll be doing

Build product data services

Engineer reliable event-driven pipelines

• Design for duplicate delivery, ordering constraints, idempotency, retries, timeouts, partial failure, dead-letter handling, backpressure, and recovery.

Protect data integrity and tenant boundaries

• You are proficient with Python and SQL where their data-processing, analytics, integration, or machine-learning ecosystems provide a practical advantage.

• You understand relational, document, graph, key-value, analytical, and object-storage models and their tradeoffs.

• You understand distributed-systems concerns such as asynchronous processing, delivery semantics, concurrency, backpressure, idempotency, consistency, recovery, and failure isolation.

• You have experience with containers, cloud infrastructure, automated testing, CI/CD, infrastructure automation, monitoring, and production operations.

Job Title : Senior UX Designer

About Luupli :
Luupli is a social media app that has equity, diversity, and equality at its heart. We believe that social media can be a force for good, and we are committed to creating a platform that maximizes the value that creators and businesses can gain from it, while making a positive impact on society and the planet. Our team is made up of passionate and dedicated individuals who are committed to making Luupli a success.
As we scale our platform, we are seeking a Senior UX Designer who possesses exceptional design skills, a creative mind, and a deep understanding of the digital user experience. In this pivotal role, you will be responsible for creating user-centred designs that are innovative, intuitive, and enhance our product's usability.
Responsibilities :

• Leadership: Collaborate and engage in a leadership role within a team of UI/UX designers, driving the creation of intuitive, top-quality designs from conception to final delivery.

• Collaboration : Partner closely with the product, engineering, and marketing teams to align product design with our strategic objectives, user needs, and technological feasibility.

• Design Development : Produce comprehensive design deliverables including wireframes, user flows, mock-ups, and interactive prototypes to communicate design concepts and user interaction.

• User Research : Conduct and analyze user research and usability testing to gather insights, validate design decisions, and drive continuous design improvement.

• Design System : Establish and promote design guidelines, best practices, and standards to ensure a unified and consistent user experience across our product suite.

• Technical Liaison : Work closely with developers to ensure the accurate translation of designs into the final product and troubleshoot any issues that emerge during development.

•
Industry Knowledge : Remain updated on the latest UI/UX trends, techniques, and technologies and integrate relevant ones into our design practices.

Requirements :

• A bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience in UX design, Computer Science, or a related field.

• Proven track record as a UI/UX Designer, with an impressive portfolio demonstrating your creativity and skill.

• Expertise in design software (e.g., Sketch, Adobe XD, Illustrator, Figma) and basic understanding of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

• Solid understanding of responsive and mobile design principles.

• Strong interpersonal and presentation skills, with the capacity to articulate design concepts and rationale effectively.

• Experience conducting user research and incorporating feedback into design revisions.

• Exceptional attention to detail and a commitment to creating high-quality, user-centric designs.

Our Culture :
At Luupli, we thrive on creativity, collaboration, and innovation. We're looking for individuals who are problem solvers, team players, and visionaries with a strong design aesthetic. If this resonates with you, we'd love to hear from you.

Compensation
Equity-Only, Purpose-Driven
At Luupli, we believe in building something extraordinary together. This role is equity-only at this stage, meaning you’re not just working for Luupli, you’re building it with us. If you’re driven by impact, excited to shape the future of social media, and ready to share in the upside of what we’re creating, this is your chance to be part of the founding story.

Notice to Recruitment Agencies
Luupli does not accept unsolicited CVs or candidate profiles from recruitment agencies. We do not enter into contracts or pay fees for candidates submitted without a prior written agreement in place. Please note that any CVs received in this manner will be considered the property of Luupli, and no fees will be payable.

postings.title: Backend Engineer Internship
postings.descriptionText:
Overview: Supply Chain API and Microservices Development
The Backend Engineer is a hands-on role responsible for the development, scaling, and maintenance of the core API services that power our entire integrated platform. You will build highly reliable, secure, and performant backend services within the NestJS modular monolith, focusing on critical supply chain logic, complex payment integrations, and the orchestration backbone for our AI agents.

Internship Details
Duration: 3 months

Start Date: Immediate

Location: Remote
Stipend: None initially. Based on your first-quarter performance, you may be offered a paid full-time opportunity, or even be absorbed directly by the client as an FTE.

Key Responsibilities & Core Projects
You will own the backend development for the most complex domain logic, ensuring scalability and transactional integrity.

• API Development & Implementation: Design, develop, and deploy highly scalable APIs for all platform components using Node.js 22 and NestJS within the TypeScript modular monolith. This includes the backends for the e-commerce checkout, internal tool APIs, and the B2B portal.

• SCM Domain Logic: Implement complex, transactional business logic within the core supply chain modules: Order Management (OMS), Warehouse Management (WMS), and Manufacturing Execution (MES). Ensure data integrity using PostgreSQL 15.

• Integrations & Payments: Implement secure, reliable integrations with third-party payment gateways and external shipping/logistics providers.

• Performance & Reliability: Implement effective caching strategies using Redis to boost API performance. Design and implement asynchronous processing and event-driven workflows to ensure system reliability and handle high-volume operations.

• Security & Monitoring: Ensure all services adhere to security standards (JWT authorization, API security). Integrate backend services with the observability stack (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Loki) for monitoring and tracing.

Required Technologies & Tools
Candidates must possess deep, hands-on experience with our core backend and data stack:

• Core Backend: Expert proficiency in Node.js 22, NestJS, and TypeScript (mandatory).

• Data Layer: Strong expertise in PostgreSQL 15 (schema design, query optimization) and utilizing Redis for caching.

• Architecture: Experience designing and implementing APIs (REST/GraphQL), asynchronous communication, and event-driven patterns.

• Workflow: Experience working within a Monorepo structure, contributing to CI/CD via Makefile, and utilizing Docker for local development.

AI Agent Focus
You will build the reliable, secure services required for AI agent orchestration.

• Agent Orchestration: Develop the backend services and API endpoints necessary to securely orchestrate, manage, and scale the AI agent systems.

• Data Access Services: Implement secure, high-performance services that allow AI agents (using frameworks like LangChain) to access and write necessary data to the WMS/OMS modules without compromising transactional integrity.

Success Metrics & Career Path

Performance will be measured by:

• Service Reliability: Uptime and stability of deployed services, achieving defined SLOs.

• Code Quality & Efficiency: Delivery of clean, well-tested, and performant code that scales effectively.

• Feature Velocity: Timely and efficient delivery of complex backend features, particularly within the critical OMS and WMS modules.

Mentorship Structure: Reports to the Technical Architect or Engineering Lead, working directly with Frontend, QA, and SRE teams to deliver high-quality supply chain functionality.

postings.title: Senior UX/CX Designer
postings.descriptionText:
About Blueprint

Blueprint is a technology solutions firm headquartered in Bellevue, Washington, with teams across the United States. We help organizations turn complex challenges into meaningful outcomes by connecting strategy and execution across AI, cloud, data, product development, and emerging technology.

Our culture is built by people who care deeply about doing exceptional work. We set high standards, take ownership, and continually challenge ourselves and one another to be better. We work hard, support each other, and take genuine pride in what we deliver for our clients, partners, and teams.

At Blueprint , you’ll work alongside talented people with different experiences, expertise, and perspectives. You’ll have opportunities to take on meaningful challenges, expand your skills, and see the impact of what you build.

Bring your perspective. Raise the standard. Build what matters.

About the Role
As a Senior UX/CX Designer , you’ll join our client’s U.S.-based Experience Strategy & Design Studio. It’s a small, horizontally structured team that brings strategy, design, and research together around customer experience. The team is building an internal AI experiences hub for about 10,000 enterprise users. You’ll design end-to-end experiences for it, from early concepts to working prototypes.
The team uses user-centered design as its core methodology, so you’ll already know it well. You’ll work in a fast, iterative environment with direct executive engagement, and you’ll partner with stakeholders across the organization. Success here means taking an ambiguous problem, setting a clear design direction, and delivering work at the level your portfolio shows, with minimal oversight.

What You'll Do

• Design end-to-end experiences for internal AI tools, from early concepts and task flows to high-fidelity, working prototypes

• Build and iterate quickly in Lovable using AI-assisted and vibe-coding workflows, moving work into VS Code and merging it with existing projects when needed

• Apply user-centered design methods to frame problems, identify the right questions, and connect user insights to design decisions

• Create design artifacts at different levels of fidelity, including storyboards, wireframes, journey maps, task flows, scenarios, and personas

• Use and contribute to an established design system, including UI controls, content templates, icons, form design, and navigation models

• Plan and facilitate remote and live design thinking workshops with stakeholders and users

• Present design direction and future-state concepts to stakeholders, including executives, in a clear and compelling way

• Validate work with peers, stakeholders, and users through lightweight research and usability checks, then iterate based on what you learn

What You'll Bring

• Training or certification in user-centered design or design thinking from a recognized program such as IDEO, IBM, Stanford, LUMA, or Forrester

• A Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Design, Product Design, Human-Computer Interaction, or a related field and 8+ years of product or service design experience; a Master’s degree and 6+ years of experience; or equivalent experience

• Strong UX/UI design skills demonstrated through a portfolio of shipped work

• Hands-on experience designing and prototyping in Lovable

• The ability to gather user context independently and turn it into design strategy and execution without detailed direction

• Strong communication and storytelling skills, including presenting complex concepts to executive audiences

Preferred Qualifications

• 5+ years of shipping products or delivering to customers through an end-to-end design process

• 3+ years of hands-on primary UX research experience, including planning and conducting 1:1 user interviews

• 5+ years of designing, planning, and facilitating live and virtual design thinking workshops

• 3+ years of experience in the technology sector with enterprise (B2B) customers

• Experience with VS Code, GitHub, Figma, Photoshop, Illustrator, or Sketch

Portfolio Requirements
A portfolio is required to be considered for this role. It should show your design process, your role on each project, and examples of shipped or delivered work.

Compensation
At Blueprint , we strive to offer competitive pay that reflects the value of our team members. Compensation for this role is influenced by a variety of factors, including skills, education, responsibilities, experience, and geographic market.
For candidates based in Argentina, the anticipated gross compensation range is $3,125 to $4,375 USD per month , with a midpoint of $3,750 . Please note that we typically do not hire new employees at the top of the posted range. Actual starting pay will be determined based on experience, skills, and internal equity. The final compensation and job title may vary depending on the selected candidate’s qualifications.

Location and Employment Structure
This is a full-time, remote position open to candidates based in Argentina. You’ll need to work at least 2 hours per day, Monday through Thursday, during U.S. Mountain Time business hours.
The selected candidate will be employed through Blueprint ’s applicable local Professional Employer Organization (PEO) or Employer of Record (EOR) partner and assigned to support a client engagement expected to last 18 months.
Benefits, statutory entitlements, and any additional required payments will follow the applicable local employment requirements.

Benefits

• Medical, dental, and vision coverage

• Flexible Spending Account (FSA)

• 401(k) retirement plan

• Competitive paid time off

• Professional growth and development opportunities

Benefits and eligibility may vary based on role, employment status, and location.

Equal Employment Opportunity

We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital or familial status, military or veteran status, citizenship status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

The Solution Architect is a strategic leadership role responsible for defining the complete, end-to-end technical architecture for our integrated supply chain e-commerce platform. You will translate complex business requirements across Manufacturing (MES), Warehouse (WMS), and Order Management (OMS) into secure, scalable, and compliant technical blueprints. Your designs will ensure seamless integration between all core systems and our next-generation AI agent infrastructure.

Internship Details
Duration: 3 months

Start Date: Immediate

Location: Remote
Stipend: None initially. Based on your first-quarter performance, you may be offered a paid full-time opportunity, or even be absorbed directly by the client as an FTE.

Key Responsibilities & Core Projects
You will design the technical vision for our critical business flow: MES → WMS → OMS → Payments → Invoices.

• Architecture & Design: Define the architecture (modular monolith/microservices) and API contracts for core modules (OMS, WMS, MES) built on Node.js 22/NestJS using TypeScript.

• Multi-Tenancy & Security: Define the strategy for tenant isolation using PostgreSQL 15 with Row-Level Security (RLS) and architect the JWT-based licensing and feature metering system.

• Infrastructure (IaC): Blueprint the deployment standards using Terraform and Docker with orchestration handled by Traefik on Oracle Cloud Free VMs.

• Compliance & Observability: Ensure adherence to compliance (HS codes, export controls) and design the monitoring and tracing strategy using Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenTelemetry.

• Technical Leadership: Lead architectural reviews and mentor engineering teams on domain modeling, performance, and best practices.

Required Technologies & Tools
Candidates must demonstrate expertise in system design and hands-on integration across this stack:

• Backend/Core: Node.js 22, NestJS (Modular Monolith), TypeScript

•
Frontend Patterns: Next.js 14, React 18

• Data/Storage: PostgreSQL 15 (RLS), Redis, Meilisearch, MinIO

• DevOps/Infra: Terraform, Docker, Traefik, pgBackRest

• Security/Auth: Authentik/Ory Kratos, Vault

AI Agent Focus
You will architect the platform for integrating advanced AI capabilities into our operational systems.

• Agent Infrastructure: Design the systems for hosting and orchestrating multi-agent systems that securely access data from MES, WMS, and OMS.

• Framework Integration: Define best practices for production AI agents utilizing frameworks like LangChain, LlamaIndex, or AutoGen.

Success Metrics & Career Path

Performance will be measured by:

• Architectural Soundness: Delivery of scalable, secure, and well-documented technical blueprints.

• System Resilience: Achieving defined SLOs for the core business process flow.

• Compliance: Full and verifiable implementation of security and compliance controls (RLS, Vault).

Mentorship Structure: Reports directly to the Head of Technology/CTO, leading the architectural review board and mentoring senior engineering leads.

postings.descriptionText:
AI Researcher

About Vetto

Vetto builds the infrastructure for next-generation AI training data. We partner with the world’s top AI labs to push the frontier of what models can do — by designing, collecting, and delivering the highest-quality training data for the hardest problems in AI.
AI Researchers at Vetto figure out how to teach models new capabilities and how to tell whether it worked. You’ll design datasets and evaluations, run experiments, study model failures, and turn what you learn into better data and training strategies.
Most of our work is evaluation-driven, with some fine-tuning and post-training used to validate research hypotheses. You won’t be expected to build the infrastructure alone: you’ll work with an engineering team that builds the platforms and tools behind the research. You should still be comfortable writing code, analyzing data, and moving your own experiments forward.

Why Vetto ?

•
End-to-end ownership. You’ll take research questions from an initial idea to a dataset, benchmark, experiment, and useful conclusion.

•
Direct collaboration with top AI labs. Your work will help frontier teams understand their models and decide what data or training approach to try next.

•
Work that gets used. Your research can become training data, evaluations, technical reports, open benchmarks, and published papers.

•
A wide range of hard problems. Depending on the project, you might work on agents, model evaluations, human or synthetic data, failure analysis, or post-training.

•
Fast, flat team. You’ll ship experiments in days, not quarters.

What You’ll Do

• Design and run experiments to understand model behavior, test new ideas, and determine whether a dataset or training intervention actually works.

• Use fine-tuning and post-training experiments when useful to validate research hypotheses and measure improvements in the capabilities we care about.

• Create datasets, benchmarks, agent environments, rubrics, and evaluation methods for problems that are not well measured today.

• Work directly with AI labs and enterprise partners to turn open-ended model-development goals into concrete research and data projects.

• Dig into model outputs and trajectories to understand systematic failure modes and separate model limitations from problems in the data, grader, or evaluation setup.

• Write analysis code and build lightweight tools or prototypes for your own work, with support from engineers when a workflow needs to become reliable infrastructure.

• Share what you learn through clear technical reports, internal discussions, benchmarks, and research papers.

What We’re Looking For

Must-haves:

• Experience doing empirical research or similarly open-ended technical work with machine learning systems.

• Hands-on experience designing and running agentic systems for complex work, such as coding agents and automated research pipelines.

• Good experimental judgment: you can form a hypothesis, choose useful baselines and metrics, run a careful experiment, and make sense of noisy results.

• Strong Python and data analysis skills, plus enough software engineering ability to prototype your own research workflows.

• The independence to take an ambiguous question about a model and turn it into a dataset, benchmark, experiment, or other concrete contribution.

• Rigorous analytical thinking — you look at the underlying evidence, notice subtle failure modes, and question results that seem too simple or too good to be true.

• Excellent written and verbal communication with researchers, engineers, customers, and non-specialists.

• Comfort with ambiguity, fast iteration, changing priorities, and occasional forward-deployed work with partner teams.

Nice to have:

• Research or industry experience in LLM evaluation, post-training, agents, human or synthetic data, alignment, or AI safety.

• Experience designing datasets or benchmarks, validating annotation quality, or working with large collections of model outputs and trajectories.

• Published research, technical writing, open-source contributions, or strong independent projects.

• Experience building or managing human feedback pipelines.

• A background in cognitive science, linguistics, philosophy, statistics, or another field that helps you think clearly about evaluation.

• Experience at an AI lab, AI data company, or in a partner-facing research role.

We care more about evidence of excellent work than any single credential. A graduate degree, publications, lab experience, open-source work, independent research, and production engineering experience are all useful signals, but none is a requirement on its own.

What We Offer

• Competitive compensation and a stock option plan.

• Global, remote-first work with flexibility and periodic in-person on-sites every few months.

• Direct collaboration with cutting-edge AI labs on evaluation, data, and post-training challenges.

• High ownership and fast career growth in a founding-era team.

Location: Global / Remote, with periodic in-person on-sites every few months
Reports to: Co-founders

Job Description
Maisha Meds is hiring! We’re seeking an engineering manager to manage our wonderful engineers to build technology to improve healthcare in Africa.

About Maisha Meds

Maisha Meds is an organization dedicated to improving health care in Africa through best-in-class technology.

Founded in 2017, Maisha Meds has created the largest digital network of private pharmacies and clinics across Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Nigeria, and Zambia through our mobile software. Our platform not only helps these providers improve business by making sales, managing inventory, and tracking patients. It also reimburses them for providing high-quality care for malaria, family planning, and HIV prevention at discounted costs.
Maisha Meds logs millions of patient visits every year and has provided hundreds of thousands of reimbursements to date. We harness data from our network of pharmacies and clinics to reveal health and market trends, which allows us to design better solutions that work for the people we serve. We have worked with leading academic institutions such as UC Berkeley, Emory University, and KEMRI to evaluate the effectiveness of our programs. Research shows that our system is able to significantly increase the uptake of long-acting contraceptives and appropriate malaria case management.
Our work is funded by a range of partners including scale-up funding from USAID Development Innovation Ventures and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. This will help Maisha Meds greatly expand its mobile software to 7,500 total pharmacies and clinics by late 2026, delivering subsidized care to nearly a million new patients in the process.

About the role
Maisha Meds builds a point-of-sale Android app for pharmacies to track their sales and manage their inventory and leverage AI to improve directions of use for medicines. On top of the Android app, we have a layer of features to help us run patient programs so that patients visiting pharmacies can receive subsidized care. We also built a suite of back office tools to help our operational staff manage the subsidy programs. postings.title: Ingeniero de desarrollo Mina subterranea
postings.descriptionText:
Quiénes somos



AngloGold Ashanti es una compañía minera global de oro con una cartera diversificada de operaciones de alta calidad, proyectos y actividades de exploración en 10 países a lo largo de cuatro continentes. Buscamos constantemente oportunidades para crear valor a través de otros minerales, apalancando nuestros activos, habilidades y sólida experiencia en el sector.



En AngloGold Ashanti, aseguramos un entorno de trabajo significativo que genera resultados tangibles, entendiendo que nuestra labor trasciende la minería:





• Impacto Social y Económico: Construimos medios de vida en las comunidades, defendemos una gestión ambiental responsable y fortalecemos las economías tanto locales como nacionales.


• Cultura Colaborativa: Nuestros líderes y equipos están comprometidos con la escucha activa y el apoyo mutuo, valorando la diversidad y promoviendo la equidad en cada acción.


• Bienestar Integral: Estamos convencidos de que la excelencia solo se alcanza cuando priorizamos el bienestar de cada persona y fomentamos comportamientos basados en el respeto.





Sobre Cerro Vanguardia



Cerro Vanguardia es una empresa minera argentina dedicada a la exploración y tratamiento de oro y plata en la provincia de Santa Cruz. Desde 1998, funciona como un motor de desarrollo regional, promoviendo la explotación responsable de recursos y el crecimiento de comunidades como Puerto San Julián. Su misión se centra en generar valor para sus empleados y accionistas garantizando un ambiente seguro y protegido.



Conozca más sobre nuestra visión, propósito y valores - AngloGold Ashanti




Visión general del puesto:

Contribuir al desarrollo seguro y eficiente de la mina subterránea mediante la planificación, coordinación y supervisión de las operaciones de avance y preparación. La función implica asegurar el cumplimiento de los diseños mineros, programas de producción y estándares de seguridad, optimizando la utilización de recursos, la productividad y la disponibilidad de los frentes de trabajo. A través del liderazgo en terreno, el seguimiento de indicadores y la mejora continua, se busca garantizar el cumplimiento de los objetivos operativos de la compañía.

Propósito del rol:

Asegurar la ejecución segura, eficiente y conforme al diseño de los planes de desarrollo y preparación de la mina subterránea. Coordinar los equipos de trabajo, supervisar el ciclo completo de desarrollo y controlar el cumplimiento de los programas de avance, calidad, productividad y seguridad, manteniendo una fuerte presencia en terreno.

Principales responsabilidades:

- Planificar y coordinar los desarrollos y preparaciones de mina conforme a los programas diarios, semanales y mensuales.

- Supervisar en terreno el ciclo completo de desarrollo, garantizando el cumplimiento de los estándares operativos y de seguridad.

- Coordinar los equipos de trabajo y asegurar la disponibilidad de frentes para perforación, voladura, sostenimiento y extracción.

- Verificar que rampas, galerías y accesos se ejecuten conforme a los diseños, secciones, direcciones y pendientes establecidos.

- Controlar la calidad de las voladuras, el avance efectivo y los niveles de sobreexcavación.

- Identificar restricciones operativas, analizar desviaciones y establecer acciones correctivas para asegurar el cumplimiento del plan.

- Realizar el seguimiento de indicadores de avance, productividad, disponibilidad de equipos, tiempos de ciclo y costos.

- Coordinar actividades con las áreas de Planificación, Geología, Geotecnia, Perforación y Voladura, Mantenimiento, Servicios de Mina y Seguridad.

- Participar en análisis de riesgos, investigaciones de incidentes y acciones de mejora continua.

- Liderar técnicamente a supervisores y operadores, promoviendo el cumplimiento de procedimientos y estándares de seguridad.

Requisitos obligatorios:

-Título universitario de Ingeniero/a de Minas.

- Experiencia de 3 a 5 años en minería subterránea, preferentemente en ingeniería de desarrollo.

- Experiencia en operaciones mecanizadas, desarrollo horizontal y/o vertical, perforación y voladura.

- Conocimientos de sostenimiento, carguío y transporte, ventilación y servicios de mina.

- Conocimiento e interpretación de diseños y planos mineros.

- Manejo de software de planificación y diseño minero, como Deswik o Datamine.

- Conocimientos de indicadores de avance, productividad, utilización y disponibilidad de equipos.

- Experiencia en coordinación de equipos operativos y supervisión de actividades en terreno.

- Conocimientos de gestión de riesgos críticos y estándares de seguridad en minería subterránea.

Cualificaciones deseables:

- Liderazgo en terreno y capacidad de gestión de equipos.

- Planificación, organización y orientación a resultados.

- Capacidad analítica y resolución de problemas.

- Toma de decisiones operativas.

- Comunicación asertiva y escucha activa.

- Trabajo interdisciplinario.

- Proactividad y orientación a la mejora continua.

- Fuerte compromiso con la seguridad operacional.

Condiciones de la posición:

- Modalidad de trabajo bajo diagrama 12x9.

- Jornada laboral de 7:00 a 19:00 horas, turno diurno.

- Contratación efectiva.

- Posición con fuerte presencia en terreno e interacción permanente con las áreas operativas y técnicas de mina


Beneficios y Compromiso con el Colaborador y la Comunidad



Cerro Vanguardia prioriza la calidad de vida y el bienestar integral de sus colaboradores, ofreciendo iniciativas orientadas al desarrollo, salud, apoyo familiar y fortalecimiento del ambiente laboral. Entre las principales acciones se destacan programas de vínculo familiar, monitoreo ambiental participativo, asistencia integral al empleado, bienestar personal, asesoramiento técnico y gestión de liderazgo.



Además, la compañía brinda acceso a servicios especializados de salud, apoyo psicológico, nutricional y asesoramiento profesional para empleados y sus familias, reforzando su compromiso con un entorno seguro, colaborativo y sostenible. Los programas e iniciativas están sujetos a las políticas internas y criterios aplicables de Cerro Vanguardia.



Declaración de Igualdad de Oportunidades de Empleo



Estamos transformando la minería con una cultura de equidad, inclusión y respeto. Valoramos a cada persona y creemos que la diversidad de historias, ideas y perspectivas impulsa nuestro crecimiento.

postings.title: GTM AI Engineer
postings.descriptionText:
About Customer.io

Over 9,000 companies — from scrappy startups to global brands — use our platform to send billions of emails, push notifications, in-app messages, and SMS every day. Customer.io powers automated communication that people actually want to receive. We help teams send smarter, more relevant messages using real-time behavioral data.

About the role

Hi, my name is Nick Guardino, Senior Director of Marketing Ops at Customer.io , and I'm looking for a GTM AI Engineer to help take our AI agents from scrappy prototypes to production-grade systems our GTM teams can depend on.

Over the last 3.5 months, our GTM AI team has built 11 agents now running in production, serving 120 active users and roughly 25,000 tool calls a day — all through custom CLIs that work, but weren't built to scale. We believe businesses can run leaner and go further when they deploy AI agents well, and we're figuring out that motion in real time. This role owns the scale and reliability layer so the rest of the team can keep building.

What we value

• Craft over quick wins — energized by making things robust, not just making them work.

• A point of view — we want someone who asks "why did you build it that way?" and has a specific answer for what to do instead.

• Comfortable being wrong — you try things fast, and you course-correct just as fast.

• AI-native by default — you'd rather direct Claude to write and QA code than write it by hand.

What you'll do

• Alpha-to-production ownership — take newly built agents from working v1 to production-ready: write evals, harden prompts and tool definitions, and refactor prototype scaffolding into clean, production-quality code.

• Observability & stability — instrument tracing, logging, and monitoring across the agent fleet so we catch regressions before our 120+ GTM users do.

• Deployment & infrastructure — stand up and maintain the pipelines that get agents into users' hands without surprises, owning environment parity and release hygiene on our GCP stack.

• Database administration — own how agents read from and write to our databases, safely and at scale.

• Fleet maintenance — monitor agent behavior in production, triage issues, and ship the steady stream of improvements that make an agent indispensable rather than just useful.

• Partner closely with the GTM AI team — free up our agent builders to stay in their zero-to-one wheelhouse while you own scale and reliability.

• Bring an outside point of view — tell us what we built wrong, and back it up with a plan to fix it.

What we're looking for

• 4+ years in software engineering, platform/infrastructure engineering, or a similarly technical role, ideally at a B2B SaaS company.

• Comfort working in the terminal daily, with a real GitHub PR-and-deploy workflow.

• Cloud hosting experience — Kubernetes, VMs, or equivalent; Google Cloud experience strongly preferred.

• Experience with how agents interact with and edit databases, including some hands-on database administration.

postings.descriptionText:
About us:

Airtm is a financial-infrastructure company building the future of the online-work economy. We are on a mission to empower the world's growing number of Digital Entrepreneurs in the Global South, giving them the financial freedom to thrive.

The problem is clear: in emerging markets, accessing the dollar economy is difficult. Cross-border payments are slow, expensive, and often lose value to inflation. This limits the potential of millions of talented individuals.

Airtm’s solution is a swift and comprehensive financial platform that facilitates low-value cross-border payments and local cash-outs. As pioneers in stablecoin-payment infrastructure, Airtm has built the most advanced cross-border payment system available on the market.

As a company married to the world of online work, Airtm will go beyond payments to build the necessary infrastructure the online-work economy needs to thrive. We are fostering an entirely new economy, giving individuals, communities, and countries the tools to take control of their financial destinies.

About the Role

We're looking for a Head of Security to build and lead security at Airtm, reporting to the VP of Engineering. You'll own the security posture of the systems that move people's money across borders, from application code and cloud infrastructure to identity, vendors, and incident response. You'll set the strategy, build the team and the practices around it, and stay hands-on enough to make the hard technical calls yourself.

Our stack is TypeScript/Node.js microservices on Kubernetes (AWS), with React front ends, organized into autonomous product teams. Security here works as an enabler embedded in how teams ship, not a gate at the end. AI-assisted development is core to how we build, so you'll be expected to use AI tooling fluently for security work, and to define how we adopt AI agents and LLM-powered systems safely.

Key Responsibilities

•
Security Strategy & Roadmap : Define and own a risk-based security strategy for a financial platform; prioritize investment by real threat and business impact, and report on posture to executive leadership and the board

•
Incident Response : Own detection, response, and recovery for security incidents; maintain runbooks, lead incidents and post-incident reviews, coordinate with forensics, legal, and communications, and turn every incident into lasting improvements

•
Application Security : Embed security into the SDLC with threat modeling, secure design reviews, SAST/DAST/dependency scanning, and secure coding standards that engineers actually adopt

•
Cloud & Infrastructure Security : Partner with Infrastructure to harden AWS, Kubernetes, networking, and CI/CD pipelines; own IAM and least-privilege access, secrets management, and security in Terraform and GitOps workflows

•
Detection & Monitoring : Build the detection and alerting capability that finds malicious activity early, across application, infrastructure, and access logs, and tune it to keep signal high

•
Crypto & Key Security : Own the security model for key management, wallet and custody operations, and the blockchain integrations our payment rails depend on

•
Fraud & Account Security Collaboration : Work with Product and Risk teams on account takeover, abuse, and transaction-level controls

•
AI Security : Define guardrails for AI coding tools and for AI agents and LLM pipelines we build or deploy, including agent permissions, prompt injection, data exposure, and tool-access boundaries

•
Compliance & Assurance : Own our security compliance program (SOC 2 and related frameworks), audits, and customer and partner security questionnaires, aiming to make compliance a byproduct of good engineering rather than a separate burden

•
Vendor & Third-Party Risk : Run vendor risk assessments and security due diligence for partners, investors, and acquirers

•
Vulnerability & Patch Management : Establish clear SLAs by severity and keep remediation moving across teams without becoming a bottleneck

•
Team Building & Mentorship : Hire, grow, and lead security engineers; build a security champions network inside product teams; raise the security bar across all of engineering

•
On-Call & Escalation : Participate in and help shape the security escalation path for production incidents

Required Qualifications

•
8+ years of experience in information or application security, including 3+ years leading security teams or functions

•
Demonstrated experience leading incident response for real, high-stakes incidents, including coordination with external forensics and counsel

•
Strong knowledge of AWS security and Kubernetes security (IAM, network segmentation, RBAC, secrets management, container and image security)

•
Hands-on experience with application security in a microservices environment: threat modeling, secure code review, and dependency and supply-chain risk

•
Experience building detection and monitoring capabilities (SIEM, log analysis, alerting; Datadog or similar)

•
Experience owning or leading a compliance program such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, or PCI-DSS, including audit cycles

•
Ability to read and review TypeScript/Node.js code and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform); you don't need to be a full-time developer, but you need to be credible with engineers

•
Experience securing CI/CD pipelines and software supply chains

•
Hands-on experience with AI-assisted tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot) for security work, and a clear point of view on the risks of AI-generated code and agentic systems

•
Strong communication skills; able to explain risk to engineers, executives, regulators, and customers, and to write policies and runbooks people follow

•
Sound judgment under pressure; able to make fast, defensible calls with incomplete information

Nice to Have

•
Background in fintech, payments, remittance, or crypto environments, especially key management, custody, and blockchain security

•
Experience with fraud, account takeover, and abuse prevention

•
Experience securing AI agents and LLM-powered systems in production (prompt injection defenses, tool-permission models, eval and red-teaming approaches)

•
Hands-on offensive security experience (penetration testing, red teaming) or running bug bounty programs

•
Experience with cloud-native security tooling (CSPM, runtime protection, policy-as-code such as OPA/Kyverno)

•
Familiarity with regulatory requirements for money transmission and financial services across multiple jurisdictions

•
Security certifications (CISSP, CISM, OSCP, AWS Security Specialty)

•
Experience supporting investor, buyer, or enterprise due diligence on security posture

•
Experience building a security function from a small base in a fast-growing engineering org

What We Look For

Beyond the technical skills, we're looking for a leader who:

•
Takes ownership of security outcomes, stays calm and clear in an incident, and communicates early when risk is rising

•
Treats security as a partnership with engineers , building guardrails and paved roads rather than gates and tickets

•
Has good judgment about risk , knowing when to stop a release, when a small risk is worth the speed, and how to explain the tradeoff to the business

•
Improves the team around them , through mentorship, champions, and making secure choices the easy ones

•
Collaborates across boundaries , working with Product, Infrastructure, Legal, Compliance, and Support as one team

•
Knows when (and when not) to lean on AI tooling , and brings rigor to how we adopt it safely

Compensation
