This position is well suited for a senior full-stack developer who enjoys solving complex distributed systems challenges, takes ownership of features from design through production, and can build reliable communication solutions that perform consistently under demanding conditions.

What You'll Do:

• Design, develop, and maintain multi-channel messaging capabilities for delivering emergency notifications through SMS, email, voice, and mobile push.

• Build and maintain integrations with messaging providers such as Twilio, SendGrid, Azure Communication Services, or similar platforms.

• Develop scalable messaging architectures using queues, background workers, asynchronous processing, and message-driven systems.

• Implement reliable delivery mechanisms, including retries with exponential backoff, idempotency, deduplication, provider failover, and delivery status tracking.

• Optimize messaging workflows to support high-volume notifications reaching thousands of recipients.

• Implement and manage delivery receipts, provider webhooks, and notification tracking processes.

• Support SMS compliance requirements, including opt-in/opt-out management, 10DLC, and toll-free registration.

• Implement email authentication and deliverability practices, including SPF, DKIM, DMARC, bounce handling, and related monitoring.

• Develop mobile push notification capabilities using Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) and Apple Push Notification service (APNs).

• Design data models and workflows for recipient audiences, groups, multilingual message templates, and notification delivery tracking.

• Develop and maintain backend services using Node.js, GraphQL, MySQL, Redis, and publish/subscribe technologies such as MQTT.

• Contribute to frontend development using Vue 3 or React to support notification management and operator-facing interfaces.

• Integrate with third-party mass-notification systems and support directory and roster synchronization.

• Deploy, maintain, and troubleshoot containerized applications using Docker, Kubernetes, and Helm.

• Write automated unit and end-to-end tests, maintain CI workflows using GitHub Actions, and participate in code reviews.

• Use AI coding agents to support development productivity while reviewing and validating generated code.

• Collaborate with Engineering and product stakeholders to define technical solutions and deliver reliable, maintainable production features.

What You Bring:

• 7+ years of professional software development experience, including experience delivering and supporting at least one production software product.

postings.title: Marketing Lead
postings.descriptionText:
Marketing Lead
Role type: 1099 independent contractor, full time Location: Fully remote, LATAM

About First Principles

First Principles is a product consultancy founded by startup and enterprise product leaders. Our focus is AI-first product management training. We help enterprise product and technology teams put AI to work in the jobs they already do, responsibly and productively. Almost every large company is trying to solve this problem right now.
Our programs are customizable, not custom. Clients choose from a catalog of practitioner-led classes across AI foundations, AI-first product management, and building AI products. We shape the program around their budget, goals, timeline, approved tools, and governance rules. A program can be a few focused sessions or a full 12 to 16 week certification. It can run virtually, on-site, or as a mix of both, for cohorts ranging from dozens of people to a couple hundred.
So far we have run three cohorts for Elsevier Health and a product and design focused program for another enterprise client. We also just launched a hybrid program with a national healthcare company. Healthcare is where we started, not where we plan to stop.

The Role
You will be our first dedicated marketer, and you will own marketing for the training business from strategy through execution.
The job starts with making us look like the firm we actually are. That means a website, materials, and proof that hold up in front of senior enterprise buyers. From there, you build a top of funnel that gives our sales team real conversations to work with. You keep a steady rhythm going, measure what works, and cut what does not.
We want a brand that stands on the firm itself, not on any single person's voice. That brand rests on three things: our client results, our program, and the many practitioners who design and teach it.
We teach AI-first product work, so our marketing has to show that we practice it. We expect you to use AI heavily to research, produce, and adapt content, and to keep messaging consistent across channels. But our website, content, and strategy cannot read like AI slop. AI can do a lot of the heavy lifting on production. You make the calls on the story, the positioning, and what ships.
This is not a role where someone hands you a plan. You tell us what success looks like, how you will get there, and then you get it done.

Responsibilities
Website. Own our website end to end. It is a modern code-based site, not a drag-and-drop builder, and you will maintain it yourself using AI coding tools such as Claude Code or Codex. Your first big project is to:

• pivot the site to be training-first

• bring it up to date with how our programs work now: flexible length; virtual, on-site, or hybrid delivery; and the "customizable, not custom" framing

• own conversion paths, forms, page speed, SEO basics, and analytics

Positioning and packaging. Work with the people who design and deliver our programs to turn a broad catalog into a few clear program shapes that are easy to describe, compare, and buy. Then write the language that goes with them.
Proof. Build a library of case studies, outcome data, and testimonials from the programs we run, within what our client agreements allow. Proof is our strongest marketing asset, and today we have published far less of it than we have earned.
Sales enablement and lead magnets. Partner with sales on the materials they use and the offers that start conversations. That includes the pitch deck, one-pagers, sample curricula, proposal templates, and lead magnets that give a product leader something genuinely useful. Sales brings what buyers are asking for. You bring the craft to make it sharp.
Channel mix. Define which channels we invest in and why, then execute. Shift the mix as the data comes in.
Measurement. Own our signal metrics, such as website traffic, engagement, followers, email list growth, inbound leads, and meetings sourced. Share a short weekly report. Run small, fast experiments and tell us plainly what is and is not working.
Budget. Own a monthly budget in the four to low five figures for tools, ads, materials, events, and outside specialists when you truly need them. Within that budget, you decide how to spend it. You do not need sign-off on every line item.
Partnership with sales. Work side by side with sales on target accounts, campaigns, follow-up, and messaging. They will tell you what they hear from buyers, and you will turn that into material that helps them close.
Know the space. Build and keep current your understanding of three things:

• how product teams work

• how AI is changing their work

• where enterprises are getting stuck on AI adoption

Our team will help you get up to speed.

Requirements

What We're Looking For
A marketer who builds and ships. Five or more years in B2B marketing. That includes time as a first or only marketer, or on a small team where you owned both strategy and execution. You have marketed high-consideration services or software to enterprise buyers.
An excellent writer with taste. You write clearly, cut filler, and can tell when something sounds generic. Please come ready to share strong marketing writing you have produced.
Hands-on with AI tools, including coding agents. You are comfortable using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or similar tools to make real changes to a website. You use AI across your work to move faster on research and production. You also know where AI makes the work worse, and you catch it.
Comfortable with measurement. You can set up analytics, tracking links, and a basic CRM pipeline, and you can build a simple dashboard that shows whether something is working.
Self-directed. There is no marketing manager above you. Experienced product leaders on our team will give you context, feedback, and hands-on support. But you set the plan and drive it.
Understands enterprise buyers. Our buyers are senior product and technology leaders at large companies, and they expect polish as a baseline. As a small firm, we need to be noticeably better than that baseline to stand out.
Near-native English, C2 minimum. Written and spoken. Senior US enterprise leaders will read everything you produce.
Available for US-aligned hours. You need consistent overlap with US business hours.

Nice to Have

• Marketing experience in professional education, corporate training, learning and development, or consulting

• Familiarity with how product management and software teams work

• Design skills (Figma or similar) and basic video editing

• Account-based marketing experience

• Experience with modern static site frameworks such as Astro, Next.js, or similar

• Experience marketing to healthcare or other regulated industries

Benefits

Compensation and Logistics

• Engagement type: 1099 contractor

• Location: Fully remote, LATAM

• Working hours: US timezone overlap required

• Compensation: Commensurate with experience, designed to compete with top-tier remote compensation

Technical Skills

postings.title: RevOps Project Manager (Part-Time) for a European B2B Agency
postings.descriptionText:
About Paired

Paired is a global staffing and recruiting agency that specializes in pairing remote work with top-tier talent!
We are dedicated to connecting talented individuals with remarkable companies in need of their skills. Our goal is to create fulfilling job opportunities for professionals around the world.

The client
Advertising and consultancy services company working with RevOps infrastructure for B2B teams. They build the systems that make growth work.
The founder has reached the point most agency founders reach eventually. Their days are full of client emails, chasing the team, managing delivery risk and keeping projects from slipping. None of it is optional and all of it is in their head. The problem is not only the hours it eats. It is that managing risk and creating growth are opposite modes of thinking, and they cannot do both well in the same week.
They're hiring the person who takes operations off them.

Why this role is part-time, and what it becomes
Right now there genuinely is not forty hours a week of work here. We are coming out of a contraction and back into expansion, and they would rather hire someone part-time and pay them properly than hire full-time and have them sitting idle, which is unfair to both of us.
The plan is that this grows. Part-time now, full-time as the client base expands, then Head of Operations. They're not dangling that vaguely: they'll will set out the milestones, what hitting them does to your compensation, and roughly when they expect each step. You should hold them to it.
What they're asking for in return is commitment. If you take this and a full-time offer appears a month later and you disappear, it damages us. If you are doing one other part-time role alongside this, that is fine and I understand it. What I do not want is someone juggling five clients who gives this one the leftovers. I have seen fractional done badly and I would rather pay for focus.

What you will own

Client and stakeholder management

• Be the operational point of contact for our clients, so that I am not

• Keep every client informed, handle the back and forth, and escalate to me only what genuinely needs me

• We currently run around four clients at once, a mix of large and small projects. Six is the most we have ever carried. As we scale, the model is roughly one project manager per five clients

Project delivery

• Own timelines, scope and deliverables across those accounts

• Know the status of everything without being asked, and chase it when it slips

• Spot delivery risk early and bring me a proposed fix rather than a problem

Team coordination

• Keep the team pointed at the right work and hold them to what they committed to

• Run the follow-up so that nothing dies in a thread

Revenue operations

• Keep our pipeline, CRM and reporting accurate and current

• Build and tidy the systems and automations that hold delivery together

• Turn what is currently in my head into documented, repeatable process

Requirements

Who this is for

• You have done revenue operations or operational project management in an agency or client services environment, and have carried multiple accounts at once

• You are comfortable being the operational face to clients. This is a stakeholder-facing role, not a back-office one

• Excellent written English. We work with international clients and are moving into the US market

• You are organised to the point of being slightly annoying about it, and you follow through without being chased

• You can work independently. There is no operations team to lean on. For a while, you are it

• You want this to grow into something bigger, and you are willing to commit while it does

Who this is not for

• You are a fractional operator running five clients and this would be number six

• You want a purely strategic seat. For now this is hands-on: emails, trackers, chasing, process writing

• You need a manager checking your work

• You are looking for full-time immediately and would leave the moment one appeared

Benefits

• Part-time, remote, on a contractor basis. We will agree the weekly hours and the working pattern together, but you will need reliable overlap with Barcelona for client calls and with the team. If you are in Latin America, your mornings cover our afternoons, which works well, and it positions us for the US clients we are moving towards.

• Growth path for full-time and Head of Operations role

• Compensation for part-time up to USD1.5k/month

What success looks like

• The founder stops being the person clients email first

• Projects land on their dates, and when they will not, they hear it early with a plan attached

• Our operations run on documented process rather than on my memory

• The founder spends his weeks on expansion instead of firefighting

postings.descriptionText:
This is a remote position.
A high-volume story-discovery and production role that turns raw human experiences found on social media into compelling short documentaries for large audiences.
Organization: Confidential client in the media sector
Location: Remote – open to candidates anywhere in the world (candidates in Palestine and the wider region are especially welcome)
Role Type: Full-time (40 hours/week)
Schedule: Fully remote with flexible, non-timebound hours.

The opportunity Our client is looking for a producer who can discover an extraordinary human story and help the person behind it tell it to the world. Sometimes that starts with a TikTok, a comment or a passing reference to something someone has lived through. Your job is to recognize the bigger story, get in touch, build trust, interview them and guide them through filming the footage that brings it to life, then work with editors to turn it into a compelling film of roughly ten minutes for YouTube and Snapchat.

About the organization

Our client helps the 99% be seen by empowering people to tell their own stories, because traditional media focuses on the 1%. The team has published almost 8,000 videos, filmed by people themselves on their mobile phones and remotely guided through the process. Its channels cover mental and physical health and survivor stories.

What you will do

• Discover original human stories across TikTok, other social platforms and online communities, using social search, AI-assisted research and emerging tools to find promising contributors.

• Run high-volume outreach: the team works toward roughly 30 contacted sources per day, knowing that around one in ten converts to a signed content license agreement and interview, with a goal of three published stories per day.

• Assess whether a story has the depth, access and visual potential to become a strong film, and convince contributors to take part.

• Research and verify stories rigorously: check claims against documented evidence, make sure health stories match documented symptoms, and keep survivor stories safe from legal risk, working through checklists with a QC layer above you.

• Conduct thoughtful interviews that uncover specific experiences, meaningful moments and a clear narrative.

• Remotely direct contributors to film themselves and their everyday lives on their phones, using clear filming briefs written for people with no production experience.

• Develop story outlines and edit scripts with strong hooks, progression and a satisfying ending, and work with editors to shape interviews and user-generated footage into compelling films

• Read retention and performance data from platform dashboards and use it to improve story selection, structure and delivery.

What you bring

• At least three years of relevant experience in journalism, interviews and developing human stories, including remotely directing contributors and producing user-generated content.

• Genuine fluency in US culture and social media: you know what is on the pulse with American audiences right now, especially Gen Z, and how to cater content to it, not just how the platforms work.

• A thorough understanding of TikTok, YouTube, Snapchat and Facebook, and experience structuring unscripted content for social audiences.

The developer accounts, build pipeline and release tracks don't exist yet, so that's where you begin, and you stay on the same app through its public launch on the App Store and Google Play.
Sprints run two weeks with four to five features each, and coding agents write most of the first draft. You review every diff, add the tests the agents missed, and make the calls on sync, storage and releases. If you'd rather have a QA team or a release manager handle testing and store submissions, this probably isn't the right seat.
You report to the studio's leadership and work day to day with the lead developer and a backend developer, who's your counterpart on the sync and upload APIs. You'll also write risk notes and tradeoffs directly to the client team, with your recommendation attached. Success means sprints that close with their acceptance criteria verified, a write queue that neither loses nor doubles a submission on real devices, and an app live on both stores where sync failures show up in monitoring before anyone reports them.

You'll:

• Set up Apple and Google developer accounts, signing, CI builds and testing tracks

• Build the local storage, write queue and retry logic that keep the app working offline

• Agree the sync and upload APIs with the backend developer, and decide how conflicting edits resolve

• Build phone-number sign-in with SMS codes, and push notifications that fall back to SMS

• Build camera capture and e-signature flows that save each signed record as a new version

• Measure and improve startup time, memory and app size on low-end Android phones

• Handle store submissions, privacy disclosures and review rejections, and add crash and sync monitoring

You Bring:

• 4+ years building mobile applications, including React Native applications released on both the App Store and Google Play

• Offline-first work you built yourself: local storage, queued writes, retries and conflict handling

• Performance tuning on low-end Android, with startup time or memory measured before and after a change

• Daily use of Cursor, Claude Code or a similar AI coding tool on production mobile work, with TypeScript, automated tests and CI around it

• Clear written and spoken English for PR descriptions, risk notes and tradeoff explanations to a client team

• Experience working from written acceptance criteria, and the judgment to push back on a merge that misses them

Bonus Points:

• An in-app e-signature or document flow that stored versioned records

• An application built for field, frontline or hourly workers

• A localized application, or Spanish for testing the interface

• Backend work such as writing an endpoint or a database migration

• Crash reporting or sync monitoring you set up and then used to fix a problem seen in the field

What's Offered:

• Fully remote contractor role from LATAM, full time at about 40 hours a week

• Core hours in US time zones, overlapping with the lead developer and the backend developer

• One app to own, from the first project files through public release on both stores

• Sync, storage and release decisions that are yours to make, with a backend developer as your counterpart

• A team where AI coding agents are part of the daily workflow, with typed code, automated tests and CI in place

Interview Process:
1️⃣ Intro Call: 30 minutes with atomic✳HR on your background and goals
2️⃣ Leadership Screening: A short call, possibly with an async part first
3️⃣ Product and Developer Conversation: How you take features to merge and agree sync APIs

• Experience connecting, managing, and maintaining APIs for generative AI platforms within a marketing data architecture

What’s Offered:

• Remote role with the flexibility that comes with a distributed, async-friendly team

• Competitive compensation based on experience and location

• A pivotal, high-visibility seat on a scaling Data & Analytics team, with real ownership over the agency's reporting infrastructure

• The chance to build the data backbone for an agency whose partners are education and nonprofit organizations working to build a better world

• A culture built around finding a better way, playing as a team of A-players, and treating results as the engine rather than the goal

2️⃣ Screening Call with Atomic HR

postings.title: Creative Strategist (Freelance)
postings.descriptionText:
Job Description: Creative Strategist

Role summary
YAMU Media is hiring a Creative Strategist to own the creative side of paid media for a pod of 5 to 8 clients. You decide what gets made, write and direct it, and use what the ads do in market to decide what gets made next.
This is a hands-on role. You write the scripts (using AI to draft at volume, then editing by hand), find and brief the talent, give direction on raw footage, and guide the editors and designers. You also read the performance data yourself and set the priority list for new creative, so the work stays tied to results.

What you'll own

•
Write scripts. Turn the creative angle, customer research and past winners into hooks and full video scripts for each client. Write every hook, re-hook and call to action, and make each script easy for talent to deliver and easy for an editor to cut.

•
Source talent. Find, vet and book the creators and on-camera talent each client needs, and keep a bench of proven people so new concepts can start quickly.

•
Direct talent. Brief talent before the shoot, give clear direction on delivery and on-camera performance, and give specific notes on the takes you receive.

•
Direct raw footage. Review raw footage, choose the usable takes and moments, and tell editors which hooks, lines and sections to build the cut around.

•
Direct the creative team. Brief editors and designers with a clear goal, reference and success measure for each asset, and give written feedback that gets to a finished ad in as few rounds as possible.

•
Analyze creative performance. Read ad-level results for each client, work out why ads won or lost (hook, angle, format, talent, offer), and write down what to repeat, iterate or retire.

•
Set creative priorities. Decide what the team makes next for each client and in what order, balancing iterations on proven ads against new concepts, and keep that list current as results come in.

Using AI to write scripts at volume
You will use AI to draft far more scripts than one writer could produce by hand, and you will be the editor who decides what is good enough to shoot. AI is the first draft. You are the final say.

•
Draft in volume. Use AI to generate many hooks and script variations from the creative angle, customer research, offer and past winning ads.

•
Vary on purpose. Ask for different angles, hook types, formats and lengths, not many copies of one idea, so each batch gives the pod something real to test.

•
Edit every script by hand. Nothing goes to talent or the client without a human read. You cut, rewrite and sharpen each draft so it sounds like a real person talking, fits the brand and is easy to perform.

•
Check every claim. AI can invent facts, results and testimonials. You verify each claim, number and promise against the client's own materials, and you keep scripts within platform ad policy and any client or legal rules.

•
Build the system. Maintain the prompts, reference documents (research, personas, offer, past winners) and script templates your pod uses, and improve them based on which drafts get approved and which ads perform.

•
Close the loop. Label each script by angle and hook type, so performance data shows what to ask AI for next.

•
Know when not to use it. Some concepts, especially ones that depend on a personal story or a delicate topic, are better written by you from scratch.

Writing modular scripts
Every script you write is built from interchangeable sections, so one shoot can produce many ad variations and we can test one element at a time.

•
Write in blocks. Build each script from labeled sections: hook, setup, body, proof, offer and call to action. Each section should work on its own and connect cleanly to the others.

•
Write several hooks and CTAs per script. Pair multiple hooks with the same body, and multiple calls to action with the same close, so editors can mix and match from a single set of footage.

•
Keep sections self-contained. Avoid lines that only make sense in one order, such as references to something said earlier, so any hook can be swapped in without breaking the flow.

•
Brief talent for swaps. Have talent record each hook and CTA in more than one take and in a consistent tone, framing and pace, so the pieces cut together without a visible seam.

•
Name every module. Give each hook, body and CTA an ID and record which combination went into each ad, so results can be traced to the specific element that won or lost.

•
Lock compliance in its own modules. Keep approved claims, required disclaimers and disclosures in fixed sections, and re-check any new combination before it goes out.

•
Use AI on the modules. Ask AI for fresh hook and CTA variations against a body that already works, then edit and approve the ones worth shooting.

Platform and regulatory compliance
Some of our clients work in regulated industries, such as health and wellness, supplements, financial services, legal services, and credit, housing or employment offers. You are the first line of defense: every script and creative direction you give must be written to pass Meta and Google review and to stay within the rules that apply to the client.

•
Know the platform rules. Keep current on both Meta's and Google's advertising policies, including Meta's special ad categories, Google's restricted categories, and the limits each sets on health claims, personal attributes, before-and-after claims, misleading claims and sensitive topics. Write scripts that stay inside both so ads are not rejected and accounts are not restricted. Policies change often, so check them again before each new batch of creative.

•
Know the client's industry rules. For each regulated client, learn the claims, disclosures and disclaimers their industry requires, and write them into the script and the on-screen text, not as an afterthought.

•
Substantiate every claim. Do not write results, savings, health benefits or guarantees that the client cannot back up with documentation. Follow advertising rules on endorsements, testimonials and paid creators, including clear disclosure of paid relationships.

•
Brief talent on what they cannot say. Give creators and on-camera talent a plain list of prohibited claims and required disclosures, and review raw footage for off-script statements before it goes to editing.

•
Get approvals in writing. Route scripts and final ads for client sign-off, and for the client's legal or compliance reviewer where the client requires it. Keep a record of what was approved and when.

•
Hold AI drafts to the same standard. AI tools do not know a client's compliance rules. Check every AI-drafted line against them before it moves forward.

•
Escalate, don't guess. When a claim or format is unclear, raise it with the Traffic Manager and the client instead of publishing and hoping.

You are not expected to give legal advice. You are expected to spot risk early, follow the client's compliance guidance, and bring in the client's legal or compliance contact when needed.

What success looks like

•
First 30 days: you know every client in your pod, have read their research, offer and best-performing ads, and have shipped your first scripts with talent booked for the next shoot.

•
First 60 days: each client has a written creative priority list you maintain weekly, a repeatable brief your editors and designers work from, and a shortlist of talent you have worked with.

•
First 90 days: you run the full loop for your clients without help: analyze results, set priorities, write, direct and hand off. New creative ships on schedule, and you can show which ads came from which learning.

What you bring

• Experience writing direct-response video scripts and hooks for paid social, with examples you can show.

• A track record of reading ad-level performance data (hook rate, CTR, CPA or ROAS, frequency) and turning it into clear creative decisions.

• Experience directing on-camera talent or creators, in person or remotely, and giving useful notes on raw footage.

• Experience briefing and managing editors and designers, and giving feedback that is specific and kind.

• Comfort in Meta Ads Manager and a reporting tool such as a spreadsheet or dashboard.

• Clear writing and good judgment about what to make first when everything feels urgent.

• Reliable follow-through across several clients at once.

• Hands-on experience using AI tools to draft and iterate on scripts, and the editing skill to turn those drafts into ads that sound human.

Nice to have

• Experience with UGC and creator-led ads for ecommerce or lead generation clients.

• Familiarity with creative testing frameworks and with how Meta delivers and fatigues creative.

• Basic editing skills, enough to rough-cut a hook or mark up a cut.

• Experience working inside an agency with several client accounts.

How the role fits
YAMU Media organizes client work into pods. Each pod is built for 5 to 8 clients and pairs a Traffic Manager with a Creative Strategist, supported by video editors and designers. You are the creative lead of your pod. The Traffic Manager owns media buying and the client relationship; you own what the ads say and show.
You will work every week with the Traffic Manager on what the data says, with editors and designers on production, and with talent on shoots. You report to Account Manager.

postings.title: Engineering Manager
postings.descriptionText:
About Onfleet

Onfleet 's mission is to power the future of commerce by enabling businesses of all sizes to move goods more efficiently and delightfully. Our product includes intuitive smartphone apps for drivers, a powerful modern web application and dashboard for logistics teams, and automatic notifications and real-time tracking for recipients. Onfleet powers millions of deliveries every week for thousands of businesses around the world across a range of industries, from grocery and prepared meals to pharmacy, flowers, and furniture.

About the role

Onfleet is hiring an Engineering Manager to lead one of our cross-functional product teams: four to seven engineers, working closely with a product manager, reporting to the CTO.

We are looking for a leader who drives execution without being on the critical path. You own the team's people, delivery, hiring and process. You delegate, coach through growth and through tough moments, act early, proactively and fairly, when something is not working, and keep execution visible with data and metrics rather than feelings.

We code through agents, and a core part of this job is coaching the team's agentic way of working. We are not hiring the smartest person in the room. We are hiring the person who makes everyone else work smarter.

How We Work

We code using agents, and 100% of our code is written this way. Generating code is the easy part. Knowing what good looks like, and holding the bar, is the job. For a manager this means coaching engineers in how they plan, direct, review and verify agent work, ensuring there’s a balanced approach and vigilance towards quality, and pushing the team's workflows forward as the tools evolve. An engineering manager at Onfleet holds a high bar, shepherds the team's execution, keeps the quality of our releases high, and does it with the team rather than trying to be the hero who does it all.

Every engineer helps improve how we work instead of only following it. The manager sets that tone: you drive the direction and make room for the team to challenge it.

We are candid and have a low ego. Challenge us on how we run engineering, and expect to be challenged back.

What you'll do:

•
Lead a team of four to seven engineers. One-on-ones, honest feedback, career growth, and early, fair action when something is not working.

•
Own delivery. Plan with the team, keep commitments visible, remove blockers, and represent the team in planning and product meetings.

•
Partner with product. Work with your product manager daily on priorities and the trade-off between roadmap and technical health.

•
Coach the agentic way of working. Pair with engineers on how they plan, direct and review agent work. Guide, sometimes push, the direction, and bring in what works on other teams. Help the team evolve with our tool-set and best practices.

•
Stay hands-on, off the critical path. Code through agents, review pull requests, and keep your technical judgment current. Delivery never depends on your personal output.

•
Hire and grow the team. Run structured hiring with our process, and develop the engineers you already have.

•
Hold the quality bar. The team that builds a feature owns its quality; your job is to keep that true. A flaky test is a failing test.

•
Use data. Delivery and quality signals guide your coaching and process changes. You actively use metrics to understand your team. A metric is a conversation starter, not a verdict: it tells you where to look and what to ask. You read the numbers together with what you see and hear in the team.

What You’ll Bring (required):

• 3 or more years managing software engineers who formally reported to you: you hired, ran their one-on-ones, wrote their reviews, and owned the performance decisions. Tech-lead or coordination experience without a reporting line does not count, whatever the title.

• 5 or more years of hands-on professional software development before or alongside managing.

• Proven and fluent daily use of AI coding agents, shown by what you have built: your own orchestration flows, agents or skills, or deep tuning of a team’s existing setup. Experience driving a team’s adoption of agentic workflows, beyond permitting them.

• A track record of coaching engineers through growth and through tough moments, including acting early on underperformance.

• A track record of running a team’s delivery end to end: your team shipped products to production, you were accountable for the commitments, and you can give concrete examples of finding and fixing a bottleneck.

• A track record of raising a team’s quality bar and keeping it raised: developer-owned testing and gates that hold without you policing them, with evidence you can point to, such as fewer escaped bugs, production observability, fewer production incidents, or a quality practice that outlived your time there.

• Experience partnering closely with product management on priorities and trade-offs.

• Excellent written and spoken English, roughly C1 level, and experience working day to day on an international team.

Nice To Have:

• Experience from more than one role on an engineering team, for example developer, SDET, QA Analyst / manual tester, or Scrum Master.

• Experience leading and improving agile ceremonies and team delivery practice.

• Our stack: TypeScript, Node.js, React, Rust in an AWS ecosystem.

• Experience managing a remote team spread across time zones.

• Logistics, delivery or marketplace domain experience.

• Coaching quality practices: developer-owned testing, test-driven development mindset, refactoring, observability.

Location and Benefits:

• Remote, open to candidates based in the United States, Canada or Latin America.

• The team works on US Pacific Time. You'll need to reliably work a schedule that frequently matches US Pacific business hours (9am to 5pm PT).

• Flexible PTO (paid time off).

• Laptop and work-from-home setup stipend.

• Monthly technology stipends (internet and AI tooling).

Onfleet is an Equal Opportunity Employer

Onfleet 's culture is one that strongly values diversity in its workplace and we are committed to working with potential team members who can bring diverse perspectives and experience to our company and culture.

We do not make hiring or employment decisions on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, sex, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other basis protected by applicable local, state or federal law.

We highly encourage members of underrepresented groups to apply and we will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Compensation

• For candidates located in Latin America, the base salary range is $90,000 to $120,000 USD per year.

• For candidates located in Canada, the base salary range is $140,000 to $190,000 CAD per year (about $100,000 to $135,000 USD).

• For candidates located in the United States, the base salary range for this role is $145,000 to $175,000 USD per year.

Where an offer lands within the range reflects the depth and experience a candidate brings to the role.

How we hire

You need an identity-verified LinkedIn profile to apply. That's the free "Verified" badge, the shield icon next to your name. We check for it, and applications without it don't move forward.

Before any offer, we verify your identity and work history. That includes a live video ID check and reference calls. We use AI, automated systems, and a person to review applications: every application that meets the requirements is also read by an engineering leader or a recruiter. If you misrepresent your identity or experience, the process ends.

If you need an accommodation at any step, including the camera or the ID check, tell us in your application or reply to any of our emails and we will arrange it.

Your Role:
The Web Analyst is a key member of the agency's Data and Analytics team, owning the web analytics and pixel deployment architecture that everything downstream depends on. You'll implement tracking via Google Tag Manager, troubleshoot setup issues across every paid ad platform the agency runs, and make sure data collection from client websites is airtight, from the first click through to CRM entry. Reporting to the Data and Analytics Manager, you're joining at a pivotal moment — the agency is scaling its roster of education and nonprofit partners, and this role is instrumental in evolving the tracking workflow that keeps every campaign measurable and every report trustworthy.

You'll:

• Own tag management & deployment — deploy, configure, and maintain pixels, tags, and scripts in Google Tag Manager (native templates and Custom HTML); build and maintain data layers with the Web Services team; manage GTM container structure, triggers, and variables across a multi-client environment; implement server-side tagging where it improves measurement accuracy and durability

• Support documentation & cross-team enablement — maintain tagging plans, naming conventions, and QA checklists; translate business requirements from account and client teams into functional tracking solutions; document technical setups so internal teams can interpret and rely on the data

You Bring:

• 3+ years of hands-on tracking or web analytics experience in a marketing or agency environment

• Intermediate experience with GTM containers, trigger and variable creation, data layer implementation, and server-side tagging

• Practical experience planning, deploying, and troubleshooting conversion tracking across major ad platforms, with working knowledge of pixel and Conversion API (CAPI) configuration for Meta, Google Ads, TikTok, and LinkedIn

Bonus Points:

postings.descriptionText:
Company Overview
Our client is a remote product studio that builds MVPs and custom software for startups and companies past the idea stage. Clients hire them for a fixed-scope MVP or for a product team billed by the two-week sprint, and the whole team uses AI coding tools every day.
They've been at it since 2020 and were profitable in 2025, with a 30% net margin. After building their own AI systems, they tripled monthly revenue with the same team size. Clients rate them 4.9 out of 5 in verified reviews, and the startups they build for have raised more than $25M in venture funding.

Your Role
You'll join the team building workflow software for one of the studio's clients: a live product that needs new workflow features while the existing ones keep running. The client's own engineers commit to the same repo, so every new table, permission and workflow goes in next to code someone else is changing. The weight is on the server side, from the SQL database on Azure up through the API, and you also build the React and TypeScript screens that sit on top.
AI coding tools draft most of the specs, tests and migrations. You direct them, read every diff line by line, and answer for what merges. If you'd rather write most of the code by hand, this probably isn't the right seat.
You report to the studio's leadership and work day to day with the lead developer and the product manager, who sets the acceptance criteria for each sprint. Success means delivering four to five features per two-week sprint, each verified before merge, and owning one area end to end (such as the task engine or the legacy migration) without breaking a live feature.

You'll:

• Extend the production SQL database on Azure with new tables, permissions and versioned records

• Write the server-side workflow rules: state machines, approval gates and independent review steps

• Enforce role-based access by company and assignment at both the database and the API

• Build the audit log, stale-write protection and idempotent endpoints so a retry never duplicates data

• Build the React and TypeScript work queues, bulk assignment tools and dashboards

• Integrate email, SMS and file storage providers, and design the sync APIs the mobile application calls

• Write migrations from legacy sources, with reconciliation reports and a duplicate review step

• Break each sprint's scope into small PRs and verify every acceptance criterion before merge

You Bring:

• 4+ years building full-stack web applications and releasing them to production

• Experience working in a codebase you didn't write, learning its conventions before changing it

• Hands-on work on workflow software where different user roles see different data, with approvals, task queues or state machines and an audit log or versioned history

• React, TypeScript and SQL on Azure, including schema design and migrations

• Daily use of Cursor, Claude Code or a similar AI coding tool on production work, with tests and CI behind it

• Clear written and spoken English: PRs that say what changed, why, and how it was tested, and tradeoffs explained to another team's engineers

• Experience delivering in fixed-scope sprints with branches, code review and feature flags

Bonus Points:

• Work in a regulated setting such as finance, health or insurance

• A migration from a legacy system, with reconciliation and duplicate review

• Time as an outside vendor committing to a client's repo

• Project rules, custom prompts or agent setups for AI coding tools that your team adopted

•
Spanish, since the platform is bilingual

What's Offered:

• Fully remote contractor role from LATAM, full time at about 40 hours a week

• Core hours in US time zones, so your day overlaps with the lead developer and the product manager

• An area of the product to own end to end, with your schema designs reviewed by the lead developer and the client's engineers

• A team where AI-first delivery is already the daily routine, with tests, CI and feature flags as part of the normal process

•
A start in early November

Interview Process:
1️⃣ Intro Call: 30 minutes with atomic✳HR on your background and goals
2️⃣ Leadership Screening: A short call, possibly with an async part first
3️⃣ Product and Developer Conversation: How you take features from acceptance criteria to merge
4️⃣ Take-Home Test: One feature like the real scope, built and checked

• Support User Acceptance Testing (UAT) by preparing scripts, guiding business users and capturing feedback.

• Include basic security checks in your testing, such as access control, input validation, session handling and the OWASP Top 10, and escalate findings to the security team.

• Track and report on QA metrics such as test coverage, pass rates, defect trends and defect leakage.

•
Manual testing experience. 3+ years in manual QA, testing web applications and APIs in an Agile environment.

•
Test case design. Strong at writing structured test cases using techniques such as boundary value analysis, equivalence partitioning and state transition.

Security awareness. Working knowledge of the OWASP Top 10 and how to check for common issues during manual testing.

Nice to Have:

• ISTQB Foundation certification (Advanced Test Analyst a plus).

• Hands-on use of Burp Suite or OWASP ZAP for basic security testing.

• Some exposure to test automation (Playwright, Selenium or Cypress), even if it isn't your main focus.

• Background in a regulated sector such as fintech, banking or healthcare.

• Experience with accessibility testing against WCAG 2.2.

One-liner
Own paid growth for a book of Single Grain clients as their performance strategist, and build the AI workflows that take build-outs, reporting, and QA off your plate.

About the role
Single Grain combines marketing services, software, and AI. This seat runs paid search, paid social, and programmatic for an assigned set of client accounts. You still get your hands in the accounts; your agents do most of the production. Clients treat you as their growth strategist: you tell them what to test next, and you tie spend to pipeline and revenue, not ROAS screenshots.
You should be an advanced AI user. The platforms already run on automation (Performance Max, Meta Advantage+, smart bidding); you know when to trust it and when to override it. On top of that you build your own agents for build-outs, pacing, reporting, creative iteration, and QA, and you check their output before it touches client spend.

What you will own

• Diagnose each client's paid program; set baselines and targets (CAC, ROAS, CPL, qualified pipeline, revenue) and own the plan.

• Run and optimize accounts across Google, Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, and programmatic within approved budgets.

• Ship test cycles fast: from idea to first readout in under five working days.

• Run an account health + QA agent on every account: weekly pacing, anomaly flags (spend spikes, broken tracking, disapprovals), and next-test recommendations.

• Run AI creative iteration: generate ad and landing-page variants, test them, and keep a human brand and claims check before anything goes live.

• Lead client strategy calls and bring proactive recommendations every month.

• Report monthly in terms a GM would use: spend tied to pipeline and revenue, with baselines.

• Write runbooks so the work does not depend on you being at the keyboard.

What success looks like

• By day 30: client diagnoses done; baselines and targets agreed; your account health + QA agent is live on your accounts and at least one teammate runs it on an account they own.

• By day 60: test cycles running on every account; AI creative iteration live on at least one account; monthly reporting ties spend to pipeline or revenue.

• By day 90: launch-to-learn under five working days; at least one account showing measurable CAC, ROAS, or pipeline improvement vs baseline; a runbook another person can follow. Failure = tests still launched without a hypothesis, baseline, or readout.

• By 6–12 months: client programs hit their agreed targets; workflows do 70%+ of paid production; you have designed yourself out of the daily build queue.

Evidence we want to see

• About 5+ years in digital paid media, currently at Senior Manager, Associate Director, Director, or Head scope, and still running accounts yourself, with spend scale.

• One paid result with the metric, baseline, period, and how you attributed it.

• One AI workflow or agent you built that removed real paid production work, and what it changed.

• AI fluency you can show: the workflow's inputs, outputs, and controls, and how you check agent or platform-automation output before it touches spend.

• Client-facing strategy: examples where you set the plan, not just executed tickets.

• Steady tenure; internal promotions are a big plus (same company counts fully).

• Ideal: growth/performance agency, B2B SaaS lead gen, or multi-client experience.

What this role is not
Not a media buyer or ticket-taker. Not vendor management only. Not TV, OOH, or print planning. Not a people-manager seat. Not for occasional AI users. Not a fit if freelancing, consulting, or your own agency is your main work today.

How the process works
Application → 7 short questions sent to you by email → evidence review → live working session (diagnose an account → propose tests → measurement plan) → paid, time-boxed practical on two sample accounts with a live defense → references. Redacted or recreated examples are welcome for confidential work.

Benefits
Medical, dental, and vision; life insurance; 401(k) with 4% match; unlimited PTO; monthly UberEats; MacBook; home-office stipend/setup. Subject to plan terms and eligibility.

Apply with your resume or LinkedIn. We will email you 7 short questions; answer them yourself. AI-written answers are disqualified.

PLEASE SUBMIT YOUR CV IN ENGLISH
Advanced Paralegal or Attorney, Minnesota Workers' Compensation
Location: Mexico
Work Arrangement: Fully Remote, aligned to U.S. Central or Eastern business hours
Employment Type: Independent Contractor
Industry: Legal Services / Law Firm
Compensation: $10–$20 USD per hour
Experience: Significant, hands-on experience with Minnesota workers' compensation cases or closely related injury and insurance litigation work
English Proficiency: Strong written and spoken English

About the Company
Our client is an established U.S.-based law firm that has represented injured workers and injury victims for decades, with a focus on workers' compensation and personal injury matters.
The firm is looking to add a highly experienced paralegal or attorney to work as the right hand of its litigating attorneys.

About the Role
We're looking for a highly experienced paralegal or attorney to serve as the right hand to the litigating attorney on Minnesota workers' compensation cases (work comp and related tort claims, meaning injury claims brought against insurance companies on behalf of injured workers).
This is not an entry-level or general admin role. The ideal candidate already understands how workers' compensation litigation works and can get a case fully prepared for the attorney to argue, including making appearances on the attorney's behalf short of trial itself.
This is intended to be a long-term engagement. Because of the learning curve involved in understanding Minnesota workers' compensation law and the firm's internal processes, the firm is not looking to repeat this training with frequent turnover. There is also potential for this role to expand into related personal injury matters outside of workers' compensation.

Why This Opportunity?

• Long-term engagement with a law firm that values stability and continuity.

• Work in close coordination with experienced litigating attorneys.

• Act essentially as an attorney would on a case, short of appearing at trial.

• Potential to expand into related personal injury matters.

What You'll Do

• Prepare case files for the litigating attorney from start to finish, including legal research specific to Minnesota workers' compensation and injury law.

• Review medical records and cross-reference them against the client's account of the injury to build a complete, accurate picture of the case.

• Ensure every case meets the proper medical-legal standards required to win in front of a judge or in settlement.

• Make appearances on behalf of the attorney as needed throughout the case lifecycle.

• Work under the direct supervision of, and in close coordination with, Attorney Mark Rodgers and Attorney Jim Perkett.

• Act essentially as an attorney would on a case, short of appearing at trial.

Qualifications

Required

• Significant, hands-on experience with Minnesota workers' compensation cases or closely related injury and insurance litigation work. Candidates fresh out of school are not a fit for this role.

• Comfortable independently managing a full caseload: legal research, medical record review, case preparation, and appearances.

• Strong written and spoken English.

• Based in Mexico, Central America, or South America, with availability aligned to U.S. Central or Eastern business hours.

How Success Is Measured

• Case files fully prepared for the attorney to argue.

• Accurate, complete case pictures built from medical records and client accounts.

• Reliable appearances and follow-through on the attorney's behalf.

• Long-term commitment and low turnover.

Why Join Us
You'll join a collaborative, fully remote team that values ownership, professionalism, clear communication, and long-term commitment, working side by side with experienced attorneys.
Compensation: $10–$20 USD per hour, depending on qualifications and experience; final terms to be confirmed.
Contract Type: Independent Contractor, with contracting and payments managed through Deel.

Important Notes

• This is a legal support role, not a position to practice U.S. law independently. All work is performed under the supervision of the firm's licensed attorneys.

• Shortlisted candidates may be asked to complete a written English and legal-support skills assessment.

• Please submit your CV in English, detailing your legal education, bar admission or professional credentials (if applicable), English proficiency, and relevant workers' compensation, injury, or insurance litigation experience.

This is a fully remote position.

About the Company
Our client is an established U.S.-based law firm with decades of experience in personal injury and criminal defense representation.
The firm represents injury victims in cases such as car and truck accidents, slip and falls, premises liability, wrongful death, and dog bites, and also provides criminal defense. It works with a seasoned team of trial attorneys and legal support staff, and it is committed to professionalism, responsiveness, and strong results for its clients.
The firm is looking to grow its remote support team with legally trained professionals from Latin America.

About the Role
We are looking for a proactive, detail-oriented, and legally trained Litigation Paralegal to support the firm's personal injury litigation practice, ideally an attorney or law graduate who wants to apply their legal education and experience in a remote paralegal role.
You will support the Personal Injury Litigation Attorney with case management, discovery, filings, medical records, liens, settlement preparation, client communication, and administrative tasks, while escalating legal decisions to U.S.-licensed counsel.
This role is ideal for someone who is organized, fluent in professional English, and able to manage routine case needs independently while working under attorney supervision.

Why This Opportunity?

• Work directly with a U.S. trial law firm on active personal injury litigation.

• Gain practical exposure to U.S. litigation, discovery, medical records, liens, and settlement processes.

• Develop your case management, documentation, and client communication skills.

• Work fully remotely with U.S. Eastern Time business hours.

• Join a growing team with opportunities to learn and take on greater responsibility.

What You'll Do

Litigation & Case Management

• Assist with pleadings, discovery, correspondence, court filings, and service of process.

• Track open records requests, affidavits of service, court deadlines, and case calendars.

• Monitor cases, identify outstanding tasks, and escalate issues requiring attorney attention.

Medical Records & Documentation

• Request, organize, and track medical records and billing statements.

• Follow up with providers and prepare medical treatment and billing summaries.

• Identify missing documentation and maintain complete case files.

Liens & Settlement Support

• Conduct lien lookups and coordinate Medicaid requests.

• Track medical liens, balances, and settlement obligations.

• Prepare settlement distribution statements and closing documents for attorney review.

Client Communication & Administration

• Communicate with clients, providers, insurers, opposing offices, process servers, and government agencies.

• Draft routine correspondence and follow up on outstanding documents and requests.

• Maintain electronic files, case notes, calendars, and expense records.

• Assist with filings, service fees, incoming correspondence, and other case-related administrative tasks.

Qualifications

Required

• 5+ years of relevant legal experience.

• Law degree from a recognized university in Mexico or another Latin American country; licensed attorneys are encouraged to apply.

• Advanced written and spoken English proficiency.

• Strong legal research, drafting, organization, document review, and deadline-management skills.

• Ability to manage multiple cases independently and provide accurate status updates.

• Reliable internet, a private workspace, and commitment to confidentiality and information security.

Preferred

• Experience with a U.S. law firm, personal injury litigation, or civil litigation.

• Knowledge of discovery, pleadings, court filings, service of process, and litigation calendars; Georgia procedure experience is a plus.

• Experience with medical records, billing, liens, and settlement documentation.

• Familiarity with MyCase or similar case-management software.

How Success Is Measured

• Accurate case files and timely completion of assignments.

• Reliable calendaring and deadline tracking.

• Consistent follow-up and professional communication.

• Accurate documentation and proactive litigation support.

• Organization, reliability, and proactive communication with the team.

Why Join Us
You'll join a collaborative, fully remote support team that values ownership, professionalism, clear communication, and continuous professional development.
The firm offers hands-on exposure to U.S. personal injury litigation, close work with experienced trial attorneys, and opportunities to grow your expertise in litigation support.

Important Notes

• This is a paralegal and legal support position, not a U.S. attorney position.

• All work is performed under attorney supervision. The position does not authorize independent U.S. legal advice, attorney representation, legal strategy decisions, or unsupervised legal practice. Substantive legal questions and settlement advice must be referred to the assigned attorney.

• The position requires strong ownership of tasks, attention to detail, and reliable follow-through.

• Shortlisted candidates may be asked to complete a written English and legal-support skills assessment.

• Please submit your CV in English, detailing your legal education, bar admission or professional credentials (if applicable), English proficiency, and relevant litigation or U.S. law firm experience.

This is a fully remote position.

What You’ll Do

postings.descriptionText:
★ PLEASE SUBMIT YOUR CV IN ENGLISH ★

Litigation Paralegal
Location: Costa Rica
Work Arrangement: Fully Remote, Full-Time (9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time)
Employment Type: Independent Contractor
Industry: Legal Services / Law Firm
Compensation: $10–$12 USD per hour
Experience: 5+ Years
English Proficiency: Advanced English (Subject to Confirmation)

About the Company
Our client is an established U.S.-based law firm with decades of experience in personal injury and criminal defense representation.
The firm represents injury victims in cases such as car and truck accidents, slip and falls, premises liability, wrongful death, and dog bites, and also provides criminal defense. It works with a seasoned team of trial attorneys and legal support staff, and it is committed to professionalism, responsiveness, and strong results for its clients.
The firm is looking to grow its remote support team with legally trained professionals from Latin America.

About the Role
We are looking for a proactive, detail-oriented, and legally trained Litigation Paralegal to support the firm's personal injury litigation practice, ideally an attorney or law graduate who wants to apply their legal education and experience in a remote paralegal role.
You will support the Personal Injury Litigation Attorney with case management, discovery, filings, medical records, liens, settlement preparation, client communication, and administrative tasks, while escalating legal decisions to U.S.-licensed counsel.
This role is ideal for someone who is organized, fluent in professional English, and able to manage routine case needs independently while working under attorney supervision.

Why This Opportunity?

• Work directly with a U.S. trial law firm on active personal injury litigation.

• Gain practical exposure to U.S. litigation, discovery, medical records, liens, and settlement processes.

• Develop your case management, documentation, and client communication skills.

• Work fully remotely with U.S. Eastern Time business hours.

• Join a growing team with opportunities to learn and take on greater responsibility.

What You'll Do

Litigation & Case Management

• Assist with pleadings, discovery, correspondence, court filings, and service of process.

• Track open records requests, affidavits of service, court deadlines, and case calendars.

• Monitor cases, identify outstanding tasks, and escalate issues requiring attorney attention.

Medical Records & Documentation

• Request, organize, and track medical records and billing statements.

• Follow up with providers and prepare medical treatment and billing summaries.

• Identify missing documentation and maintain complete case files.

Liens & Settlement Support

• Conduct lien lookups and coordinate Medicaid requests.

• Track medical liens, balances, and settlement obligations.

• Prepare settlement distribution statements and closing documents for attorney review.

Client Communication & Administration

• Communicate with clients, providers, insurers, opposing offices, process servers, and government agencies.

• Draft routine correspondence and follow up on outstanding documents and requests.

• Maintain electronic files, case notes, calendars, and expense records.

• Assist with filings, service fees, incoming correspondence, and other case-related administrative tasks.

Qualifications

Required

• 5+ years of relevant legal experience.

• Law degree from a recognized university in Mexico or another Latin American country; licensed attorneys are encouraged to apply.

• Advanced written and spoken English proficiency.

• Strong legal research, drafting, organization, document review, and deadline-management skills.

• Ability to manage multiple cases independently and provide accurate status updates.

• Reliable internet, a private workspace, and commitment to confidentiality and information security.

Preferred

• Experience with a U.S. law firm, personal injury litigation, or civil litigation.

• Knowledge of discovery, pleadings, court filings, service of process, and litigation calendars; Georgia procedure experience is a plus.

• Experience with medical records, billing, liens, and settlement documentation.

• Familiarity with MyCase or similar case-management software.

How Success Is Measured

• Accurate case files and timely completion of assignments.

• Reliable calendaring and deadline tracking.

• Consistent follow-up and professional communication.

• Accurate documentation and proactive litigation support.

• Organization, reliability, and proactive communication with the team.

Why Join Us
You'll join a collaborative, fully remote support team that values ownership, professionalism, clear communication, and continuous professional development.
The firm offers hands-on exposure to U.S. personal injury litigation, close work with experienced trial attorneys, and opportunities to grow your expertise in litigation support.

Important Notes

• This is a paralegal and legal support position, not a U.S. attorney position.

• All work is performed under attorney supervision. The position does not authorize independent U.S. legal advice, attorney representation, legal strategy decisions, or unsupervised legal practice. Substantive legal questions and settlement advice must be referred to the assigned attorney.

• The position requires strong ownership of tasks, attention to detail, and reliable follow-through.

• Shortlisted candidates may be asked to complete a written English and legal-support skills assessment.

• Please submit your CV in English, detailing your legal education, bar admission or professional credentials (if applicable), English proficiency, and relevant litigation or U.S. law firm experience.

This is a fully remote position.

postings.title: DevSecOps Engineer
postings.descriptionText:
We are looking for a Senior DevSecOps Engineer to join our GTB Tech Evolution Platform team , helping us build and operate secure, scalable and cloud-native infrastructure on AWS .
In this role, you will work closely with Platform, Security and Product teams to onboard applications onto standardized cloud patterns, improve automation and security, and drive the adoption of modern DevOps, SRE and observability practices .
You will play a key role in the evolution of our cloud platform, with a strong focus on AWS/EKS, Kubernetes, CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code and cloud automation .

What You'll Do

• Design, implement and operate secure, scalable cloud infrastructure on AWS/EKS .

• Lead the onboarding and migration of applications to standardized Cloud patterns and platform services .

• Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines and automated deployment processes using GitHub.

• Implement and manage Infrastructure as Code , particularly with Terraform.

• Drive the migration from traditional credential-based authentication towards AWS IAM/IRSA and secure identity management practices.

• Manage and optimize Kubernetes-based environments , ensuring reliability, security and scalability.

• Champion observability and SRE practices , including monitoring, logging and performance improvements.

• Work with tools such as Amazon CloudWatch and, ideally, Dynatrace.

• Promote automation across infrastructure and application lifecycle management.

• Maintain a documentation-first approach , ensuring platform processes, configurations and standards are clearly documented.

• Contribute to service catalog ownership and governance .

• Collaborate closely with Platform Engineering, Security and Product teams to deliver secure and reliable solutions.

• Identify opportunities to improve platform efficiency, resilience, security and developer experience.

What We're Looking For

•
5+ years of professional experience as a DevSecOps / DevOps Engineer .

• Strong hands-on experience with AWS / Amazon Web Services .

• Advanced knowledge of Kubernetes , ideally including EKS.

• Strong experience with GitHub and GitHub-based development and CI/CD workflows.

• Hands-on experience with Terraform and Infrastructure as Code.

• Solid experience with Docker and containerized environments.

• Strong knowledge of Linux environments.

• Experience with cloud automation and infrastructure automation.

• Experience with authentication and IAM , particularly within AWS environments.

• Strong understanding of Amazon CloudWatch and cloud monitoring.

• Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional technical teams.

• A strong security mindset and interest in building reliable, scalable and well-governed cloud platforms.

Nice to Have

• Experience with Python scripting or automation.

• Experience with Java applications or ecosystems.

• Experience with Dynatrace or other observability platforms.

• Experience with AWS IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) .

• Knowledge of SRE principles and practices .

• Previous experience working in large-scale enterprise or financial services environments.

What do we offer you?

• Full-time and permanent employment contract or contractor mode

• Remote location in Spain (other EU or Latam countries will be taken into account)

• Professional growth possibilities & learning opportunities

• Possibility to join a multicultural team & work in the international environment

• Variety of benefits to support your physical, emotional and financial wellbeing: private medical insurance, life insurance, lunch and transport card as part of the flexible remuneration pack, and online language classes

• Smart Office Pack

If you have read this far and you are looking forward to joining this challenge, do not hesitate to apply... we would be delighted to meet you!

postings.title: Marketing VA - PART TIME (TT291026PT)
postings.descriptionText:
Marketing Assistant

Location: 100% Remote (LATAM)
Schedule: Part-Time, 80 hours per month, mornings (Monday to Friday)
Contract: Independent Contractor

About the Role

There is Talent is looking for a hands-on Marketing Assistant with strong content skills. You’ll help create and publish content, prepare our newsletter, support partnership outreach, and assist with other day-to-day digital marketing tasks.

We’re particularly interested in someone who knows how to use AI tools to research, draft, and repurpose content efficiently, then edit it carefully so it is accurate, useful, and sounds natural.

This is an execution-focused role. You’ll work on priorities set by management and report on your progress. You will not be responsible for managing the marketing team.

Key Responsibilities

Content Creation

• Research, draft, edit, and publish content for LinkedIn, YouTube, and other relevant channels.

• Repurpose existing material, including podcasts, interviews, videos, blogs, and internal ideas, into content for different platforms.

• Use AI tools to support research, outlining, drafting, editing, and repurposing.

• Review and improve AI-assisted content to ensure it is accurate, clear, engaging, and consistent with our brand voice.

• Help maintain a practical content calendar and keep production on schedule.

• Prepare social media assets such as short-form videos, clips, images, and carousels, or coordinate their production when needed.

• Support our YouTube channel by preparing and publishing videos, Shorts, titles, descriptions, and thumbnails.

Newsletter

• Help plan, write, edit, and send newsletters.

• Coordinate newsletter content and any supporting links or assets.

• Track basic performance, such as opens, clicks, and engagement, and suggest improvements.

Partnerships and Outreach

• Research entrepreneur groups, business communities, associations, podcasts, newsletters, and other relevant networks.

• Contact potential partners with clear, personalized messages.

• Follow up on conversations and keep partnership contacts and next steps organized.

• Help coordinate opportunities such as guest contributions, interviews, referrals, and co-marketing.

General Digital Marketing Support

• Assist with social media scheduling and basic community engagement.

• Support website updates and basic SEO tasks.

• Help coordinate marketing campaigns and keep related materials organized.

• Track basic marketing activity and results, and share concise updates.

• Take on other general digital marketing tasks as priorities change.

What We’re Looking For

• Strong writing and editing skills, ideally supported by examples of your work.

• Experience creating content for digital channels, especially LinkedIn, video, or email.

• Confidence using AI tools for content work, with the judgment to check and improve their output.

• Experience with newsletters, email marketing, or partnership outreach.

• A working understanding of social media, content marketing, websites, and basic SEO.

• Organized, reliable, and able to manage deadlines and follow-ups.

• Comfortable taking direction, communicating progress, and asking questions when needed.

postings.title: Cloud Integration Engineer - CO
postings.descriptionText:
Resumen
Buscamos a un Ingeniero de Integración Cloud, con experiencia demostrada en despliegue e integración de tecnologías cloud open source Este rol es clave para asegurar la implementación exitosa de nuestras soluciones de infraestructura en ambientes de misión crítica, trabajando directamente con los principales operadores de telecomunicaciones en América Latina.
En este cargo tu misión será desarrollar todas las tareas necesarias, para la correcta implementación e integración de los productos comercializados por Whitestack . Estas tareas incluyen despliegue de productos Whitestack e integración de los mismos con sistemas externos sobre plataformas como Kubernetes y Openstack asegurando su correcto funcionamiento y compatibilidad con los sistemas externos del cliente.
Este rol está disponible para trabajo remoto desde las siguientes ubicaciones: México, Chile, Argentina, Colombia, Uruguay y Perú.

Responsabilidades

• Identificar y solicitar al cliente los requerimientos para el despliegue de los productos de manera oportuna.

• Despliegue de los elementos que componen las soluciones / productos de Whitestack

• Realizar testing de componentes en ambientes virtualizados.

• Realizar pruebas de validación y troubleshooting post-despliegue.

• Colaborar en flujos de trabajo tipo GitOps, con enfoque en automatización y buenas prácticas de ingeniería.

• Elaboración y actualización de la documentación concerniente a la infraestructura del proyecto.

• Análisis y resolución de posibles inconvenientes que se puedan presentar durante la puesta en marcha de los componentes a desplegar.

• Canalizar solicitudes de clientes respecto a funcionalidades de productos hacia las distintas áreas internas.correspondientes.

• Contribuir a las mejoras de los productos.

Requerimientos

Experiencia

• +2 años de experiencia demostrada en Cloud Engineering.

• Experiencia en el despliegue, integración, troubleshooting, de tecnologías cloud open source (Openstack, Kubernetes, etc.).

•
Familiarización con metodologías ágiles.

• Experiencia en configuración de redes en Linux. (Interfaces/VLAN, IPTables, enrutamiento, bonding, etc)

• Deseable experiencia trabajando con o en operadores de telecomunicaciones.

• Ingeniería Informática, Ingeniería de Sistemas, Ingeniería Electrónica, o afín.

Conocimientos Específicos / Requisitos Técnicos

•

Linux Intermedio 30%

• Comandos básicos, manipulación de archivos, red, etc.

•
Sabe aplicar configuraciones de red

•
Experiencia con Shell scripting (Bash).

•

Kubernetes Avanzado 25%

• Conoce el ciclo de vida de un pod, distingue entre los diferentes tipos de despliegues, sabe usar claims, volúmenes y storage classes, ha debugeado pods, sabe qué son probes, init-containers, ha desplegado con yaml y con Helm, etc.

•

Networking Intermedio 20%

• (Interfaces/VLAN, IPTables, enrutamiento, bonding, etc)

•

Virtualización Avanzado 10%

• Experiencia con KVM, OpenStack, o otros herramientas de virtualización

•

Ansible Avanzado 5%

• Sabe ejecutar playbooks mediante roles, conoce la típica estructura de un rol, sabe usar inventario y diferentes variables

•

Docker Intermedio 5%

• Conoce el ciclo de vida, uso de volúmenes, diferentes comandos para ejecutar, attachear, ver logs, etc.

•

Terraform Intermedio 5%

•
Ha desplegado IAC, sabe troubleshootear

Inglés: Intermedio (para leer/escribir documentación técnica)

Requisitos profesionales

• Autonomía (para lograr los mejores resultados)

•
Adherencia a estándares de clase mundial

•
Apertura de aprender nuevas tecnologías

•
Pensamiento analítico

•
Trabajo en equipo

• Disposición a participar de ventanas de mantenimiento, para intervenir sistemas de misión crítica fuera de horario laboral

Requisitos Deseables

•
Certificaciones en Kubernetes

• Certificaciones y/o experiencia en Openstack

•
Certificaciones en Linux

• Experiencia generando documentación técnica

•
Experiencia configurando equipos de red

•
Otros deseables:

•
DevOps

• NMS - Sistemas de Monitoreo (Nociones. Kibana, Grafana, Zabix, Nagios, entre otros).

Whitestack es una empresa líder en Latinoamérica especializada en soluciones en la nube e infraestructura digital híper-escalable. Trabajamos con tecnología de código abierto y los más altos estándares de la industria para impulsar la transformación digital en toda la región. Company Overview

We help talented people across Latin America land remote roles with fast-growing startups and marketing agencies in the US and Canada, and we help those companies hire people they'd never have found on their own.
